utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, would you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, and good morning to one and all. Case IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is Wednesday, the 21st of June, 2006. I'd like to welcome everybody in the courtroom. As you know, we're going to continue our proceedings. Just before the break yesterday, I asked the witness a few questions for him to be able to say specifically what the context was when he met a number of people in Prozor, and so we can now continue. I'm going to give the floor to the Prosecution to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Just to conclude with this meeting, Mr. Hujdur, yesterday during the questioning by the President, you at one stage said, and I refer in the transcript to page 135, line 25 -- from line 25. It says: "And at one point he said to his commanders, 'If you go on doing what you're doing, you will no longer get assistance from Croatia.'" I just want to confirm that I heard correctly, because this came at the end of a session.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen, that is how I understood that sentence, precisely that way. I think today, as I thought then, that it was lack of obedience towards an order and conduct towards a captured officer of the BH army, and perhaps also based on the situation he saw prevailing in town. And the general did in fact utter that sentence in an angry tone. He used swear words and words which, out of a sense of dignity towards my religion, and generally, I don't wish to repeat his exact words, but he really was very angry when he uttered that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you are referring to General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Regarding the conclusion of the meeting, in the transcript at page 136, from line 6, you say: "Unfortunately, there was a promise that the talks would continue, but the talks never continued." In the decision that was taken, was there any decision or anything concerning disarmament? What was decided regarding disarmament?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The promised meeting never took place, that's true. We returned towards Jablanica ourselves. The general remained. He stayed to talk to his subordinates and the other people present there. As to further developments, they were such that at that time the Croatian forces just entered Prozor and in several hamlets in the vicinity of Prozor, whereas the rest of the terrain remained -- well, shall we say remained free. And in the coming period that other area was under the constant -- how shall I put this? It was faced with constant ultimatums to hand over weapons and to be subordinated and attached -- or, rather, to accept the new authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: These villages, were they Bosnian or Croat villages?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we're speaking of exclusively Bosniak villages which are to be found in this area south of Prozor on the road to Jablanica, along the road towards Jablanica both on the left-hand side and the right-hand side of the road. All those hamlets and villages, just like those who -- which were to the west of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may. Just one question to make sure. You have spoken of "the Croat forces." Did you mean military of the army of Croatia or do you mean HV -- HOV -- HVO, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the operatives were the HVO, but everything was done pursuant to commands of representatives of the HV, the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: The villages that you refer to, can you name them?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. South of Prozor there was Duge, Lug, Gornja Lug, Donja Lug, Gornji Visnjani, Donji Visnjani, Parcani, Paros, Klek, Heldovi, Lizoperci, Grevici, Toscanica. That is in the south. And to the west, west of Prozor, Lapsunj, Varvara, Kovacevo Polje. Two villages east or north-east, that is Blace and Memici. They are -- they were to all intents and purposes eliminated or, rather, taken control of. And when they entered Prozor, then those settlements or hamlets were taken over. So they were already under the control of those forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And just once again for the record, which forces are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the operation, this was done by the local HVO but with full control and by the command of the representatives of the Croatian army. And I should like to add there that there were attempts to disarm the larger Bosniak villages east and north-east of Prozor - Here, Kute, and Scipe - which were their greatest problem, and that's where they made their ultimatums to -- for the people to hand over their weapons, and these ultimatums were not accepted. So those were the Bosniak villages where the -- the ultimatums were not accepted and the villagers did not hand over their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hujdur, before leaving this topic, this was the first time that you had returned to Prozor since the 24th of October, 1992, when you left. You have mentioned in your previous testimony that there was destruction which had taken place in Prozor. Did you see any of this destruction with your own eyes, or the results of the destruction in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While the general stayed on at the meeting with the people in the motel, we, on our journey back, and since all those facilities are on the main road and we passed by all these buildings on our way and were able to see that what we had written was actually how things stood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Can you give the Court an idea of the level of destruction or what kind of destruction you saw.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we saw was burnt houses, very eerie looking. We saw shop windows broken, everything looted, devastated, untidy. Everything was wrecked, and it was a terrible sight to behold compared to the situation before the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can move on to the documents, and I think, in view of the time, we, unfortunately, cannot deal with them in great detail, but I would like to touch upon some aspects of them. The first aspect relates to - and if I can refer to the transcript of yesterday, page 119, at line 13 - you referred to it was a board for the return of expulsed persons which you were a member of. The first document that I would like to show you in this regard is Exhibit number 01542. If we can show that on the e-court system. Do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, this document, it consists of two pages. If we can perhaps -- let's deal with this page first. The title of this document is, or the subject of this document is? If you can tell the Court.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just an addition here. The Board for the Return of Legal Organs and Displaced Persons, or expulsed persons, and it says Prozor, Jablanica, which means that we were in Jablanica at that town and acted -- at that time and acted from Jablanica, because this was our attempt to have the legal organs return after everything that had happened. And this document is dated February, and in the meantime a series of other events took place; the January attack on Vakuf, the situation deteriorated generally. And we asked the legal organs of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Presidency and the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the basis of information sent out previously and on the basis of the contents of this document that they should define the status for our future work so that we knew what we had to do and to give us full legitimacy in our work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Do you know who the author of this document was?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The author of this document is our team. The team compiled the document on the basis of a joint effort, and so that's the heading. Perhaps that isn't my signature. It is the signature, I believe, of one of the members. For your information, this is the signature of one of the members who was aware of all the events. It is authentic, and I can state that it is as authentic as if I had signed it, because we had decided that several members had equal right to sign documents of this kind if the others were absent or if the number one man was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: If we could go to the second page of this document and just go to the area where the author's name appears or where the signature normally appears. If we can go down a bit further. Thank you. Your name appears there as the president of the organisation, and it's signed Omer Hujdur, diploma in engineering. The fact that your name appears there without any signature, do you have any comments regarding that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say is that this is not my signature. That is true. Quite possibly the original text might have gone with the signature, but the contents of this letter, they are authentic as we sent it to the Presidency and the government. And the signature that you see there is equally valid, as valid as would have been my own, because it says above that "Signed and certified by a stamp." So this isn't something that someone could have just written on his own bat and sent out. The last sentence of the document says, "Signed and certified with a stamp." So this is an authentic document. This might be a copy from the archive. But I can say with full responsibility that the contents are authentic and that it contains all the elements of a public document. It has everything a public document should have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just with regard to the date that appears next to that signature, it's the 17th of February, 2000. Do you have any comments regarding that, or any idea?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, assumptions are probably not very valuable in court, but all I can do is assume that this man, in giving his own statement, might have placed this date and his signature there, his certification, if I could put it that way, of the authenticity of this text. So that might be it. Perhaps he didn't have access to the archives at that point and could not come by a signed document, but he found a copy and probably certified it in that way. So that is what I assume. Perhaps some of you know what actually happened, but that is my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: On that page, if we can very briefly look at paragraph 2 in the B/C/S version. And in the English version it is paragraph 3. And it says there: "... we formed, in a democratic manner, a Committee for the Returning of Legal Organs of Displaced Persons, consisting of nine members. Our proposals were that this body worked under the name of the War Presidency," and then it goes on. Is this the committee that you were referring to earlier and -- sorry, I don't have the text in front of me.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And in the fourth last paragraph on that same page, there is reference to: "Apart from forming a commission for the investigation of all relevant facts." Do you see that? Which commission does this refer to?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, when we spoke about the first document that we wrote, the first information or report sent out, we mentioned that we hadn't been -- that we hadn't established or selected this board. So that was a forum at the time. And the first document that was sent out was under the heading of a forum for displaced persons. And we asked that on the basis of the information we were sending out and on the basis of their knowledge, that an urgent commission should be established to investigate all the relevant facts and proposed measures for overcoming the situation. And that's what we reiterate here. We repeat that. We say that both from a military and political aspect or, rather, from those aspects and also from other aspects, political, military, and everything else, all the damage done there, the people killed, that the overall situation should be investigated. That's what we meant. To gather all the relevant data and information, to conduct an investigation, and to ascertain what actually happened over there. When I say "there," I mean Prozor. So that's what we repeated several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Finally on this document, if we can turn to page 1 very briefly, and if we can look at paragraph 5 on page 1. In that paragraph it states: "In spite of everything that occurred in Prozor, we initiated talks which were aimed at creating tolerable living conditions." Which talks does this refer to?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to talks held in Prozor with the general and the others. Those are the talks meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: The talks on the 1st of December that we spoke about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: If we could go to the next document. And this is Exhibit 01564. This is a long document, Your Honour, or a longer document, and if we could show the first page on the ELMO, but if I could show a hard copy and ask the usher's assistance, we do have a hard copy available for the witness. And in the e-court system, if we could go to the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the document is?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is an attempt on our part or continuity in our work along the lines of sending out relevant documents and information to the appropriate republican organs and bodies and institutions so that they should bear in mind this material and take necessary measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to how you described yesterday how your board compiled documents and reports, could you give an idea how this report was compiled, or this document, the information contained in it.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information was gathered -- or, rather, it was building on previous information gathered, updating it compared to what had already taken place. So we took statements -- or, rather, statements were taken. There was a separate commission in charge of taking statements, and later on that commission would become the commission or centre for investigating war crimes. But anyway, at this time a group of people, on the basis of standard procedure, would take statements from people who had -- who gave their statements to the commission first-hand. And some of the information would come from the police structures, and the police gathered their own information through their own channels and sources. So all this information was gathered together, and all of it is based on mostly authentic statements by the witnesses, and they were stored and kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Could you give the Court an idea of how many -- a rough idea of how many people contributed information to the commission in order to prepare these reports? Are we talking about 10 or 20 or hundreds?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: After our first information or report, each new piece of information was authentically recorded. So you would have to calculate the difference between what we had at the beginning and now. So every new case, for instance, of a house being burnt down, would be recorded, and it would be the owner of the house that had been burnt down who would have given us that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come back to this in a moment. At the bottom of that first page, it says: "Signed on behalf of the president of the board, Mr. Omer Hujdur." Is that your signature? Sorry. Obviously it's not. My mistake. What I want to ask is do you know who signed on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. He was a member our board.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Can you identify him for the Court?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, I can tell you his name, Atif Fejzic, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say yes, but ... But what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I didn't fully understand the liberty you gave me not to say names publicly. This name, however, I believe does not belong to a person who might have problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You would like this not to be mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't think that this name is important. But if it is important for the Court, I can tell you that his name is Atif Fejzic. However, my understanding was that we would not be mentioning names, that there would not be a need to mention names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall leave the name in there. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, item 2 on this first page of the document says: "List of houses that have been burnt after the entry of Croatian forces in Prozor on 24 October, 1992." If you turn to the next page of the document - and if we could have that on the e-court system, perhaps - after having had a look at that part very briefly, can you tell us what the next part of the document consists of?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question very well. Are you referring to the document about houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document consists of a number of houses burnt, with the name of the owner and a brief description of the size and value of the house, and so on. At the end, as you see, there is a stamp, and the list has been verified. The last ordinal number is 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: On which page of your document is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Page 5. If we could have page 5 up on the ELMO perhaps. While we're waiting for that, could you tell the Court how many houses are listed in this document as being destroyed or damaged.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seventy-five.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: The fact that 75 houses are listed, and with the names of owners as well, was each of these people approached to give a statement or approached with regard to their houses?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll give you a specific example. Ibro Daguda, the owner of one of these houses, a beautiful house with business premises. While his house was burning, he was inside the house. He managed to get out at the last moment. And it was these authentic experiences and actual statements about the condition of those houses on the basis of which this list and short description was compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: But once again, with regard to each of these 75 incidents, did you actually speak to -- not you personally, but members of the committee or people working for it, did they actually speak to these people? You shook your head. Could you just reply.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: In your own mind, being involved in this commission, do you have any comments or feeling with regard to - and this is from your own involvement with this commission - on the reliability of the information that has been compiled here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour. Excuse me, sir, before you answer that question. I object to that question. If he can say concretely, you know, what he knows specifically, that's fine. If he can say to some degree of reasonableness that he -- out of these 70-some houses. But I think now we're going into feelings. He can testify, as he has already, that individuals came and gave their -- gave their information. I think that's fine. As to whether he checked all this information out, that's something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Just something I would like to clarify. On line 11, page 13, I can see the figure 70 appear, I think the right figure is 75.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you answer the questions clearly without sharing with us your personal feelings. These might be important, but I would like you to first and foremost answer the question. And before giving the floor back to you, I'm a little bit puzzled. You mentioned the case of somebody called Ibro -- the name is no longer on the screen -- and I looked at the 75 names and I don't find his name on the list. Whom were you referring to when you mentioned the list of names? Which number were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Daguda Ibro, a member of our commission. He should be on the list. If he's not, it's an error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I was trying to say that the first information we drew up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I realise that Daguda Ibro is not on the list. Unless I've made a mistake. I don't see his name on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may suggest that the witness look at number 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at number 24. Yes. I can see the name Ibro, but it's not very legible. It's number 24. Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honour, may I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kruger, I think you were about to put a question, and -- to the witness and you were expecting an answer, so please put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, in light of your name appearing at the bottom of this document and that this document therefore went out under your name, were you satisfied that the information contained in this document was reasonably reliable, that you could therefore send it out under your name?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still owe an answer to a question put by the President of the Chamber concerning the discrepancy. On entry into town, a number of houses were torched, and according to the initial information, that number is smaller than the number found here. Why? Because this list was compiled in February, and between November and February a number of bad things happened. One of them was the attack on Gornji Vakuf on the 13th of January, 1993. And whenever there was an attack, a failed attack on Gornji Vakuf, the soldiers vented their anger by torching more houses. As for the authenticity of the document, it is authentic, and I would sign it right now because it was compiled on the basis of reliable information which we gathered in the way I have described. The difference or the discrepancy seen here is because the number of burnt houses and all the other misfortunes increased and grew. There was more and more destruction, killing, maltreatment, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry if I interrupt, but the Judges will have to assess all of this in a very accurate manner. If I've understood you correctly, you said as far as this list of 75 houses is concerned, some were destroyed in October when you yourself were in the cellar and then you left, and then after the month of October, because there had been this attack on Gornji Vakuf. As a result, a number of other houses were burnt down. And these house are also on this list of 75 houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until that period, yes. Until the period when we learned about the destruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Then maybe this escaped the Prosecution, but just very briefly, if you remember, on this list of 75 houses, do you have clear instances of houses that were burnt down on the 24th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. There's an error here. All these houses, all these houses were burnt when the Croatian forces entered Prozor. The list of houses burnt during the attack on Gornji Vakuf is under number 7 in this document. So I wish to correct this now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Can I ask a number of questions regarding this list. A technical question: Is there any sense behind the order in which the houses are listed? It is not alphabetic, I can see. Is there some other order behind it or is it more or less put down at random?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One might say at random or as the information arrived or as information was learnt. That's how the list was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Then I notice a difference in language. This document - and I'm bound to use the translation - speaks of houses burnt, and in one of your last replies you have used the term "torched." The result is the same, but "torch," the term "torch," at least in the English language, I seem to understand, means put to fire intentionally by someone. Are you saying that this is what happened to all of these houses or to some of them, that they were burnt down intentionally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is reliable information that speaks of intentional burning of houses, and this man who spoke about how his house was burnt is an example of this. A special kind of powder was used, but I can't recall now what it was called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Did you hear a more precise description on what was done, how this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This man described in great detail to us how it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could you tell the Bench and all present.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how authentic it will be if I tell you. It might be best to call the man who experienced this. If you're asking me to interpret his statement, the way they entered the houses was special. Some people were guarding the entrance, others were sprinkling the powder around, a third group was setting fire to it. They would start on the ground floor and then go on to the next floor up, and so on until they reached the attic. That's what I can tell you based on what the man told us, but it would be best to hear authentic testimony from the person who experienced and survived all this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: The Court certainly would not disagree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are back into open session. So let's resume now as we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: To conclude on this document, Mr. Hujdur, on the first page of the document there is reference to eight items. However, looking at the annex, it seems to me as if not all of the annexes or not all of the information relating to these eight items appears. Is this document complete?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, evidently not. All the annexes are not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: When the document was originally sent out, to your knowledge were all the annexes attached?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can move on. Yesterday, at -- in the transcript at page 123, line 20 onwards, you said: "In this information we described the situation before the attack, during the attack as we experienced it, the information we had available from the most responsible people and from our own personal experience. On the basis of this, we drew up this information signed by three people." Now, in light of this, I would like to show you the next exhibit, which is Exhibit number 01656.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, please. Before moving on to the next exhibit, could we perhaps see the B/C/S version of annex 2, please. Here in this document we can see the date 31st of August, 2000. There is a signature on there. Who signed this document? In the B/C/S document, the other pages also have the same signature and the same date, so somebody must have authenticated this document. And the Prosecution said a while ago that this document had been sent in. Can you provide an explanation for this? The Prosecution, answer this question, please. Mr. Kruger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I think it would assist in perhaps clarifying some potential confusion. This document with the signature dated in 2000, as well as some of the other annexes or documents which may we see which have later dates on them, those dates generally refer to -- or were placed on the documents when these documents were handed to the Prosecution and -- in the course of investigations. And that is most likely also the reason for this particular date and signature. At this stage I can't be more precise than that, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you don't know whether the date and the signature meet that of one of your investigators or whether it's a member of this commission who would have authenticated this document. You have no explanation to give us, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be whichever witness handed the document to us. That witness would have signed this. And that would also explain the addition of an annex 2 page to the B/C/S version, the annex 2 most likely relating to this was the second annex handed by a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, let's try to understand what's going on here. Did you hand over to one of the investigators of this Tribunal a set of documents? You personally. The documents we have here, did you hand over some of these documents personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not hand over this document to the Tribunal, but somebody from the board did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if he knows who it is it, because he's saying somebody from the board, so obviously he must know, I would like to know who that person is. The Prosecution should keep track of these -- these documents, especially if they're going to be tendering them as being authentic, accurate, and complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Ibrisimovic should know, because he just stood up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that on the list of documents we saw that the person who did this was 290 on the Prosecution's witness list and that he will be coming into the Tribunal. I think that my learned colleagues of the Prosecution can check that out, but I think that that is the person who supplied the Tribunal or, rather, the Prosecution with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So there would be another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I do thank my learned colleague for that bit of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Nevertheless, Mr. Hujdur, do you recognise the signature that has been the object of the last few minutes' debate? On the top page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you that this document be dealt with in greater detail when the witness to whom this refers comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You are not answering my question. I asked you whether you recognise this signature, and you must, I recall, answer truthfully, because you are under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do recognise it, but please, may I not -- may I be allowed not to state who that is, not to answer the question now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I suggest that we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, private session, please. I anticipated that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, if we can now turn to Exhibit number 01656. And in the -- I would like to show you the hard copy of this as well. You already have this document in the package in front of you. You will see the tab 0 -- or 1656. You first have the translation, but -- perhaps the usher could help Mr. Hujdur if he needs assistance. Thank you. Now, Mr. Hujdur, yesterday we talked about -- or you referred to information that was compiled and, "On the basis of this, we drew up this information signed by three people." Looking at this document in the light of what I've just said, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it, but may I be allowed to say that the other documents were authentic, too, regardless of who signed them. I do recognise this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an information or report on the situation in Prozor municipality before and after the brutal aggression by the HVO and HV on the 23rd and 24th of October, 1992, and the position of the Muslim people in connection with these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And if we can look at the last page, or page 12 of the document. And in the English version it is page 12 and page 13. If we can just move down a little bit. Just a little bit up. And there you see lines with the names of three people, and your own name also appears there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The original of this document was signed by all three individuals. On this document, we have one of the signatories of us three, and it is the person under number 2 who signed it. Probably during this period of time he signed his name there to certify the authenticity, but the document is authentic because it was signed by all three of the people whose names are listed here in the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the -- or this document, if we can very, very briefly look at page 2 of the document. And in the very first paragraph it starts with: "The extensive series of extreme incident causing and perfidious activities carried out by representatives of the Croatian people and after that by members of the HOS and the HVO preceded the aggression," et cetera. And then there are a number of bulleted points over the next series of pages. What do these bulleted points relate to?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those bullet points relate to the overall events, as it says in the title, before, during, and after the attack on Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: What is the source of your information, once again, for compiling this report and the information contained in it?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the events in the course of 2002 in our joint work, a number of my colleagues from the board, and it's not only the three men that stand behind this piece of information. They are the signatories, but there's a whole team of people behind this document. So a number of members of the board kept the documents and their notes and all other relevant documents which helped us to compile what happened before the -- before the attack. As for what happened during the attack, we were able to compile that on the basis of the elements that I spoke about earlier on, as well as the things that took place -- or, rather, influenced the attack on Gornji Vakuf, Jablanica, and so on when the conflict escalated, the escalation of the attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Did you sign the original of this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... people, did they also sign the original?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: You personally, having read the contents of this document and having contributed, then, to the creation, were you comfortable in your own mind about the reliability of the information contained in the document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: I want to refer you to one aspect of the document. If we go, in the B/C/S version, to page 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to clarify one point between the B/C/S version and the English version. Witness, could you turn to the beginning of the document which you can see on your screen. Could you read in your own language what you can see here. I'd like you to read the beginning of the text, and I want to check and see whether the translation into English is -- is right. It starts off with "Agresiji ..." Please read it out so that our interpreters can translate what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the aggression of the units of the Croatian Defence Council, the so-called Herceg-Bosna and the Croatian army on the -- between the 23rd and 24th of October, 1992, at 1520 -- 1525 hours on the town of Prozor where 70 per cent of the Muslims live, citizens and members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, a series of extremists incidents and perfidious activities took place carried out by the representatives of the Croatian people and afterwards the members of HOS and HVO which we mention within the context of this information and which we will endeavour to present chronologically with the taking over of power by the -- when the first multi-party elections were held and power was taken over," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So I can see that the last few words in the English text have been put in a reverse order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, but just in order to be correct. I read this out in Bosnian, and it says 80 per cent Muslims there, and it said 70 per cent in the transcript. So the witness read this out wrong, because both in the English version and in the Bosnian version it says 80 per cent, and in the transcript, based on what the witness said, it said 70 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Very well. Is it 70 per cent or 80 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I couldn't see the figure very well. So you should take what it says in the text. I'm afraid I didn't see the figure properly, and I didn't read it out properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: If we can turn to page 6 of the B/C/S version. And just before -- it's the next page. My apologies. I'm going according to the numbering on top of the document. At the bottom, just before the paragraph numbered paragraph 1. If we can move down. In the English version, or the translated version, this is on page 7, also just before item 1. Yesterday, you referred to -- or you said the following, and this was at page 130, line 1, and this was with regard to the delegation that was present at the meeting of the 1st of December, 1992: "In this delegation were people whose names you can read in that report ..." Now, from this place where I've referred you to in this document, a description of a report appears which goes on for the next two pages. Which report is being referred to in this document -- or which meeting - my apologies - is being referred to?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The report on this document refers to the meeting of the 23rd of October, 1992, when we had lengthy talks and when we thought that we had reached a good agreement, so that's the date this report refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: My apologies, I had the date wrong. How comprehensive is the description of this -- of the meeting contained in this document? If you could give us an idea on that.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how much time I have, but this is the essence, although the meeting went on for five and half hours. And I, of course, took part in the meeting. And if the President of the Trial Chamber will allow me just a minute and a half to explain what I said at the time, and the rest of us who tried in all manner of ways to overcome the difficulties in a peaceful and responsible manner without thinking of global solutions, because our presidents didn't even know what global solutions they could make. And I remember the sentence I uttered at the time: If somebody can promise us tomorrow a joint state such as Austria, for example, then if I were in that situation I would agree to that. But don't do that, gentlemen, representatives of the Croats, by force. Don't proceed that way, and don't hamper us in following what the world has already done, that is to say recognise the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as an independent state. So we're following the world. We're following the legal organs of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So allow us to act on a platform that is on a par with the work of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina given the prevailing conditions. So there were speeches of that kind on both sides. But as I say, the meeting went on for five and a half hours, and it's difficult to record everything that was said. But I do think that the contents of this are the backbone of the meeting, the succous of it, and I think that you can recognise everything that went on at the meeting; our endeavours and the endeavours of those who did not accept reasonable proposals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: In conclusion on this document, to whom was it sent?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in conclusion, that is to say on the basis of all that was said at the meeting, the conclusions that had been agreed upon should have been sent on to the War Presidency for it to verify all the matters that come under its competence and authority, and apart from that, the other organs -- apart from the Presidency, the other organs should have gone about their own business; the political parties, the army staffs, the police and everything. All of them had their part in our discussions. So it was supposed to be sent out to all those addresses whose competence and authority it was to deal with issues of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: In conclusion, I -- if I understood you correctly yesterday, this document would not have been the final report that was issued; is that correct? Was this a work in progress?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: When was this report eventually finalised, or the final version produced?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, please? I don't think I've understood you. How do you mean "when was the report finalised"? Do you mean the reports that we sent out during that period of time or do you mean this particular report from the meeting that we had? I didn't quite follow you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: My apology. The report from this commission regarding the events in Prozor. So I'm not referring only specifically to this meeting.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We sent out information on a continual basis with our requests, if I can put it that way. But this particular report or piece of information relates to the developments in the Prozor municipality or in and around the Prozor municipality. It was a continuous report, updated with new knowledge, new events, new facts, and as such it was sent on to the appropriate addresses. It's not final, but everything that happened up until that date was in there. Everything, all our demands and requests and all the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And when was the final report eventually produced? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you a specific answer when that was. There were a lot of documents, many. So as to the final report, well, it's not possible to compile that yet, not even at this point in time. But -- and here's why: Throughout that period, through our reports we informed about the people who were killed, captured, taken to camps, and those who went missing. And today, at this point in Prozor municipality, there are 62 persons, citizens of Prozor, who are still missing. We don't know anything about that. And it is the Croatian side that is responsible for them. So we can't complete the report until we learn of their fate and destiny, and that's why I say that the report is not a final one but needs to be constantly updated with that information included.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is perhaps a time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the time has come to take a break. We shall resume at ten to eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Just before we resume, I have a few questions concerning our timing. As you know, there's a witness who is supposed to testify this afternoon or tomorrow - I'm not sure - for four hours. I don't know how much time you still need, but this morning I told you that you had already had three hours, and if the Defence team need the same amount of time, there's a fair chance that we will dedicate this entire day to this witness. So we -- so we have four and a half hours left. How much time do you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have three documents that I wish to still show to the witness. I anticipate that these documents will not take much time, or as long as the other three that have been shown already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the purposes of planning, we will certainly use all the time you give us, that is the same time given to the Prosecution, but we may need a little more. I don't want to burden the Chamber in advance, but perhaps half an hour. The Defence tried to agree among themselves, but some topics are not very precisely defined. Only my colleague Ms. Nozica and I will examine the witness, and the other Defence teams may have just a question or two for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, but if I look at the English transcript, I did hear the French translation, and you said that you need the same amount of time. From what I understood, you need the same time as the Prosecution that has already had three hours, and from what I understood, you need an additional 30 minutes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, yes. Your Honour, please don't hold me to my word and take it as half an hour precisely, but it's a little more than the Prosecutor took. I can only promise that what we ask will be relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we should be able to finish this afternoon. I have just one question, and I would like to be brief. Registrar, could you show us on the screen the B/C/S page number 00920369, please. This is the last document we have seen on page 5. Registrar, this is not the right document. So this is document number 69. So here, it's up on the screen. Witness, could you read the beginning of the second paragraph, which starts off with the numbers 27/28. Could you just read out the first line, please. Could you read it out aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "On the 27th to the 28th of August, 1992, members of the HVO and HOS attacked buildings belonging to more prominent and prosperous Muslims. On that occasion, 14 buildings were damaged."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. In the report you signed, it is specified that members of the HVO and members of HOS -- of the HOS attacked. How did you establish the distinction between the members of the HVO and the members of the HOS? What was this distinction based on? So my question is a very specific question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we were still in Prozor at the time, and our delegations cooperated with representatives of the Croatian side. Their representatives said that the extreme part of the HOS and the HVO did this. That's what their own representatives told us at a meeting we had. After this, the damage was partly compensated for from the municipal budget. The authorities recognised this, and they promised to do their best to prevent it happening again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English transcript and the French translation, on the basis of that you said that at the meeting with the Croatian delegation, you were told that these were extreme members of the HOS and the HVO that launched the attack. Is that what you said? Because in the report, nobody mentions extremists in the HVO or the HOS. Could you please clarify this point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what we were told orally. However, in our report we said members of the HOS because that's what we were told, and of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: To the -- to the same passage. It is striking that this is 27, 28 August of 1992. So it falls quite outside the period of the events on which we have heard hitherto, but it is correct, it is that date. This is an isolated incident that was quite some time before the events of late October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to the Prosecutor's question I responded yesterday by saying there were at least two isolated incidents. The first was on the 26th of June, and the second is the one we are talking about now. These both took place before the events of the 23rd of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Witness, if we may turn to a next document. I would like to show you Exhibit 03020. And it is in the bundle of documents that you have at the moment. If we can have the first page up on the e-court system, please. This document dated the 30th of June, 1993, at the end also has your name to it, but I think that somebody has signed on your behalf. Could you -- do you recognise this document, or know about it?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same person who signed the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you very briefly comment on what this document is and what its purpose is.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly, if you look at the date, it's the end of June, 2002 [as interpreted]. This was a time when there were intensive attacks on Jablanica and Konjic municipalities, as well as Gornji Vakuf. The situation in Central Bosnia is known to you, but Mostar was also under intense attack. Various armies arrived in Prozor, and all their failures on these battle fronts, especially in the Gornji Vakuf area, led to the men venting their anger, because of their failures at the battlefront, on their return to Prozor. According to our information, very bad things happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It needs to be a correction somewhere. It is certainly not 2002. In the transcript it reads -- or in the document, 1993. I'm referring to line 3. Page 38, line 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That is indeed my mistake. It's a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Witness, I said -- I referred to the date incorrectly. It is indeed -- or could you confirm that it is dated the 30th of June, 1993, in the document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the original date. I'm referring to events of that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I may ask you once again, because this was sent out in your name, do you have any views or were you comfortable with the reliability of the contents of this document, the information it contained?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As in the case of the previous document, it is a result of teamwork, and I can say it's authentic or, rather, that it's contents are authentic. There is a signature and a stamp, and the content of the document is authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Hujdur, if we can move on to the next document. That would be document 03 -- or Exhibit 03907. And this is a one-page document. If we may have it on the e-court system, please. Could we have the next page, please. Thank you. Witness, once again -- sorry, this is the English version which is up on the screen. Thank you. If we can go to the bottom of the screen, where the signature and the name is. It is unclear, but can you see in whose name the document was produced?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please return it to the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you if you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It's a poor copy, so I had problems deciphering it, but I do recognise what I see now. Could you please assist me by showing me the date in the English version, because the date is not clear here. Is it August? I think it's the 3rd of August, but I'm not sure. I think it is the 3rd of August. If it's different in the English version --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Actually, the English version didn't have the 3rd, but thank you. Could you tell us what this document is, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document in which a request is made to the highest command of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to save the Bosniak men who were then on the territory of Prozor municipality, which was being held by the Croatian forces as there were large-scale arrests and men were taken to camps, all men between the ages of 16 and 60. This document is actually a request addressed to the command of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, asking them to do something about this situation. There was a war on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, if you recall a few days ago, there was some discussion of the documents and topics to be dealt with through this witness because there were discrepancies in the proofing charts, and we were told quite clearly that the witness would not testify to events in 1993. However, we know that the witness left Prozor after the events of the 23rd and 24th of October and returned to Prozor only later. Now, however, through this document, indirectly we are coming to the events of 1993. This was not presented in the proofing chart in this manner. It is in the proofing chart, but the Prosecutor did say that the witness would not be asked to deal with the events of 1993 because he wasn't in Prozor at the time. So we are not prepared to deal with this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Kruger. Defence counsel has objected to the fact that from the outset we had agreed that we would only talk about 1992. Now, this document pertains to events that unfolded in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, personally I'm not aware of the exact information that Mr. Kovacic is referring to. Does he perhaps have the -- the exact -- Your Honour, I've just had a message with regard to this, that our understanding is that this was not the agreement, that there were indeed certain aspects relating to 1993 which we -- which we undertook to -- or which we indicated would be dealt with by this witness, and this is indeed indicated in the proofing chart summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was indicated in the proofing chart, but because of the lack of clarity in referring to particular paragraphs, I raised this issue with Mr. Ken Scott, and in this courtroom we raised the issue on the first or second day after you returned from Bosnia, and we were told that the paragraphs in the proofing chart were there in error and that the witness would be examined only about events in 1992. We were told that the scope of his testimony with reference to the statement given to the OTP in February, 1992, will not include the events of 1993. Let me remind the Chamber, when we saw the discrepancy we checked this with the Office of the Prosecutor, and this was also said. We asked whether there was another statement by this witness, because when we looked at the statement, we saw that the witness was speaking about the events of 1992. However, when we saw the proofing chart, we realised that events of 1993 might be raised. So we asked whether there was another statement, because this is often the case, to see whether the witness had made any statements about the events of 1993. We were told there was no such statement, and then we asked why there are references in the proofing chart to paragraphs dealing with 1993. We were told that this would not be the topic of examination. Now, however, we see that 1993 is being referred to. This has taken us by surprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If I remember correctly -- so Mr. Scott has just walked in, and he -- as he follows the proceedings from his office, he is able to know where we stand at the moment. The Defence counsel has just stood up because Mr. Kruger wanted to put questions to the witness about a document numbered 03907 and relating to events that took place in 1993. Mr. Kovacic stipulated that when we returned from Bosnia, he had raised the issue because he had realised that in this witness's statement he only talked about what had happened in 1992, and on looking at the proofing chart, he had noticed that questions might be put relating to the year 1993, and the Defence counsel has said that they have not been able to do their preparation work and they had only prepared for the year 1992. I think this was the case, if I remember correctly. Maybe you could corroborate this. You said that you would only address issues that related to 1992. As you are here in the courtroom, you will be able to clarify this matter for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No, that is absolutely not correct. And if we go back to the transcript, at the time what I had indicated in response to questions put to me by Mr. Kovacic, both inside the courtroom and outside the courtroom, was that while the majority, substantial majority of this witness's testimony would go to 1992, there were indeed a few items in 1993. And I'm disappointed that my colleague does not recall that accurately. But I'm sure that if we go back, if necessary, to the transcript from the previous -- it would have been the Wednesday that we returned, I believe is when it was raised, and we were quite specific and I quite specifically mentioned to Mr. Kovacic why the proofing chart was different and why the additional paragraphs of the indictment had been mentioned that go into indeed 1993, and I'm confident the transcript will show that. I'm afraid, Your Honour, that there's been at least a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Notwithstanding this misunderstanding, the witness's written statement only related to 1992. On those facts which unfolded in 1993 and which are described in document number 03907, this was not mentioned in the written statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It was not mentioned in the original written statement -- sorry, Your Honour. Your Honour, you're absolutely correct. It was not mentioned in the original statement and that was indeed what caused the original discussion between Mr. Kovacic and I. Mr. Kovacic, in fairness - I believe I have this accurately - Mr. Kovacic contacted me, we discussed it, and I indeed said yes, that's correct, but my understanding was there were some limited aspect issues in 1993 that would be addressed which is in the proofing chart. The proofing chart comes after the statement. The statement was taken some years ago. In the process of the proofing and preparing the evidence for presentation in court, these additional aspects were noted, and they were indeed. And I believe if I heard Mr. Kovacic correctly a few minutes ago, he -- he concurs that the proofing chart did indeed indicate there were aspects as to 1993, if I heard that correctly. And we -- when we presented the bundle of exhibits to be presented through this witness, the 1993 documents were included as part of the bundle of documents to be presented. So I disagree that there's any surprise here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Judges who have just deliberated feel that the events of 1993 are to be found in paragraph 54 of the indictment. Therefore, the Defence team knew for some time that those events that took place in 1993 in Prozor would be mentioned. So to all intents and purposes, they should have prepared for that. We have mentioned a number of documents this morning. These documents have been authenticated by the witness, so there is no reason why we shouldn't continue putting questions to him. Mr. Kruger, so you may put your questions to the witness on this document, and in due course the Defence counsel will -- can cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, with regard to the document we are now dealing with, which is Exhibit 03907, it is still up on e-court system, this document, you mentioned that after looking at it that you then knew what this document was about, and you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a mistake in the transcript. It's the number is 03907. We seem to always have problems with numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: You were busy just briefly describing to the Court what this document was. If you could just conclude on that.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In June and July, the situation in Prozor on the territory controlled by the Croatian forces dramatically deteriorated because the male civilians were arrested, from ages ranging from 16 to 65, and they were sent to camps in Prozor first of all, and then to camps Heliodrom, Dretelj, and the other camps in Southern Herzegovina, and according to our knowledge, all the lack of success experienced by the Croatian forces on the front, all their failures, were reflected in very brutal terms on the civilian population on the territory that I spoke about. And with that knowledge, we wanted, through this document -- we called for all measures to be taken to ensure that the fate of those people should be a reasonable one, should be -- that their situation be improved. And to the end of August there was total persecution and expulsion of women and children from the territory, almost complete ethnic cleansing, and of course all this was followed by killings, planned executions, and other types of torture and uncivilised conduct where all conventions were violated, all conventions governing the codes of conduct and rules of behaviour in situations of that kind. So that was what our requests were, going up to the higher command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you. You have now broached judicial problems about conventions. If you're a legal man yourself, then that would be fine, we would welcome your point of view. But if not, then please limit your testimony to the contents of the document without making other evaluations which might be interesting for you but, as far as we're concerned, they will be dealt with in due course. Mr. Kruger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: In conclusion on this document, it's perhaps not very clear. If we can go to the top of the document. If you could tell us to whom this document was addressed.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document isn't very legible. My copy is a bad -- I have a bad copy. But it was addressed to the commander of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina because this concerned the capture of males, of men. So it was addressed to the commander of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Finally, in conclusion on this document, to your knowledge and having participated in this committee, or this board, what was your feeling on the reliability of the information contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I'm sorry, Mr. Kruger. You are again asking about feeling, and I will not take the seat of Mr. Karnavas, but I think he had a point when he raised this objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I take the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: What -- how was the information in this document compiled, just for the record?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of having listened to witnesses who told us, recounted what the situation was like, and also from other sources which can be considered reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: If we may turn to the final document, and this is Exhibit number 04247. Once again, Mr. Hujdur, this document has your name at the bottom but it appears not to be signed by you; is that correct? So if we could have the next page on the -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the document that relates to -- or, rather, is addressed to the International Red Cross and their representative offices in Jablanica. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: And do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of this document was to inform the International Red Cross about what we knew and the information that we sent on, and we sent on to them as well, and that once they become apprised of the situation that they could take steps to do what they could to improve the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: You did not sign this document. Did you participate in the compilation of this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Sorry. My question was perhaps two-barrelled. When you shook your head, was that with regard to that you did not sign the document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The contents of the document and its authenticity, the veracity of the information contained in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Hujdur, it is a bit strange that you have now looked at about half a dozen documents. On every document you are typed as the author, and in none of them you have signed. If these were copies that were filed somewhere, that's natural. One doesn't sign these. But someone else signed. Can you explain this fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are two reasons for that -- at least two reasons. All these documents, authentically sent to the addressees, were mostly signed -- were mostly signed by people who had the authorisation to do so. I signed many of those documents myself, but I don't know how it happens that these documents were pulled out, ones which I hadn't signed. I was very often in the field. I went travelling. But of course I -- everything was done with a previous agreement and consultation. So certain documents that are signed here, and they are dated 2000, were probably handed over to the investigators. So these are probably copies. They were copies, not originals. So you can check the authenticity of the documents in the original archives, and I can now confirm that they are indeed authentic documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We understood that they were copies. But the question that comes to my mind, as it did indeed to my colleague's mind, did you one day sign a document? So this kind of report or information or whatever we call it, was it personally signed by your hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Many of the reports. In fact, the majority of reports I signed myself. And you'll be able to check that out if you look into the archives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but this last document, addressed to the International Red Cross, which is a worldwide organisation, very well known to everyone, this is a request to ensure the safety of the Muslim population of Prozor and surrounding villages in the Prozor municipality, that particular document, the one we have before us. That document has not been signed by you. It is signed, but it is signed for you, not by you. Why is that? Weren't you there on the 17th of August? Were you occupied elsewhere? Because you were, after all, the president of a commission, and if one is president of a commission one does have certain responsibilities that one must respect. For example, as I am the President of the Trial Chamber, I have to sign all the Chamber's documents, except if I am absent, and then my colleague will step in and sign for me, but otherwise, it is my job to sign the documents. That is the function of a president, to sign documents. So do you have any material reason for not having signed this one? Can you tell us I wasn't there, I was absent, so wasn't able to sign the document, or some other reason perhaps? Do you have an explanation to give us for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Throughout this time we had a territory which we referred to as the free territory of Prozor municipality, with Scipe, Here, and Kute as the largest settlements, and on that territory, since it was under siege, under a total blockade, there was a great shortage of food and all other supplies. And so we had to ensure food and supplies and see that the school year goes ahead properly, and we had to go there very often, but to go there we had to go via Konjic and cross mountains, and it took us a whole day to travel to these outlying places because it was impossible to reach them through Prozor. So very often when I was going there, my deputy would sign, or the authorised person would sign instead of me. So those are the reasons for which some documents or these particular documents that have been chosen as examples were not signed by me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Still on the question of -- of signature, which -- which is a bit strange. If you look at what we see on the e-court screen, there is a hand sign left of the word "Predsjednik" and this sign, a very similar one, you find in the previous document 3020 and you also find it also in the document 01564. Do you recognise this sign? It's not on the top of the page. I'm sorry, it's on the bottom of the page on the left of the word "Predsjednik." Do you recognise this sign? Can you tell us who put it there and what its meaning is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This person, and I've already mentioned that, I gave you their name today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're back in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Kruger, in open session, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions for the witness at this time. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So that completes the examination-in-chief, and we have 40 minutes to the break, very precious 40 minutes, and I'm going to give the floor straight away to the Defence. I don't know who is going to start off with the cross-examination. I can see Mr. Murphy looking at me. Counsel Nozica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... one thing. If -- I would like to briefly come to the defence of my colleague Mr. Kovacic. I was able to locate the passage in the transcript that Mr. Scott referred to. It's on the 15th of June, at page 3293, between lines 1 and 21, and I need not take the time to read that to the Court, but I think if the Trial Chamber will take the time to look at it, I think you would agree that it gives a very clear impression that, and there are the words there "the vast majority" of the witness's statement goes to 1992, and there is a casual reference to the witness possibly at some point mentioning something in 1993. We have had now three reports in the latter stages of the witness's direct evidence dealing with the year 1993 in considerable detail, and in my submission Mr. Kovacic's point was well taken and the implication given by Mr. Scott that the Trial Chamber was being misled was unfounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We will take note of that, the difference between what was said and what was written, and we will draw the conclusions. Now, who is going to start off? I forgot one point. Just a moment, please. Mr. Registrar has just reminded me. He's always vigilant. What exhibits would the Prosecution like to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
