utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution wishes to tender as exhibits number 01542, 01564, 01656, 03020, 03907, and 04247. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll give you our ruling in due course later on. Who is going to start off? We have two counsel on their feet. That's going to be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I just wanted to tell that, under the agreement, Ms. Nozica will start and then Praljak Defence will continue, and if I may immediately inform you, Mr. Praljak will start with only two issues very shortly, and then I will continue in detail. That is the plan. The other Defences asked us only to left them couple of minutes on the end just as a reserve, if we don't cover something, they may raise one or two questions altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you. So Mr. Praljak will be asking two questions very shortly. Counsel Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before I begin, I would like the Chamber's guidelines. In the cross-examination it is my intention to mention names which are contained in the documents provided to us by the Prosecutor. I don't think there's any need that before I mention any names I ask to go into private session, but if the witness has problems with this, when he wants to say something, he can ask for private session. I would just like to make this point clear with respect to the transcript. The documents tendered by the -- presented by the Prosecution are the documents that I will deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it would be a good idea not to cite names that were cited in private session. I don't think those names ought to appear on the public transcript or record, the names that were uttered by the witness when we went into private session. So please don't mention those names. That was for very brief moments, but that applies to those names. And rest assured that as I am listening to what you're saying, I always have the time to ask that we go into private session if the need arises. Having said that, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. All I wanted to say is this: The reason why I asked to be able to mention all the names in open session, publicly, is for the following reason: We saw that the Prosecution presented a series of documents which, as the witness said, were addressed to the official organs of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Presidency, the other organisations, international organisations, and so on and so forth, and if it wasn't a problem for those names to be mentioned then, then I see no reason why there should be a problem in me mentioning them here in court today, especially as I am taking this risk upon myself. I'll do myself -- my best to take care not to mention any other names publicly, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hujdur, my name is Senka Nozica. I am Defence counsel for Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel speak into the microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a few questions, mostly on what you said yesterday and today during your testimony in examination-in-chief. May we start off by establishing very specifically or, rather, can you tell me to the best of your recollections when the HVO was established in Prozor, or when do you know that the HVO was established in Prozor?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, I would say that the official promotion was conducted in August, but everything they did and the term they used --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you when do you know that the HVO was officially established. You explain this in your statement. You say that that was the 5th of August, do you, 1992? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Officially speaking. But that term came to be used much earlier on, straight after the 10th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. After the 10th of April. Now, can you explain this to us: I must admit that there are many things that are not quite clear to me. When was the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people established? If I may, yesterday you spoke -- you said that sometime in April or May you were invited -- I think it was March or April -- that you were invited to go to the Crisis Staff although you were not a member of the SDA. Can you tell me precisely when the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people in Prozor municipality was formed?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, at the end of February and beginning of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. The end of February and beginning of March, 1992. Were you a member of the Crisis Staff at all?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member, but at the beginning of April, from the 10th of April, I was invited to attend the meetings that I spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, when the staff of the Territorial Defence of Prozor municipality was established, to the best of your recollections, and who formed it?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff, the first staff of Territorial Defence of Prozor municipality was formed on the 20th -- or, rather, 28th of March, and I think the Crisis Staff set it up. Yes, the Crisis Staff set up the Territorial Defence Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You mean the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As far as I'm able to understand you, you say for the first time, the first staff. Well, did the Territorial Defence Staff, was it set up again at some other time?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. After that date, the 15th of April, which was the deadline for a united defence staff of Prozor municipality be set up. The decision was taken between the 15th and 16th, and that's what was supposed to happen over the next few months. We were supposed to work towards that end. But as we did not, then the Territorial Defence Staff had to be established again. A new organisation with a new man at the head.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell us who the first commander of the Territorial Defence Staff was and who the second commander was, and when did that second -- when was that second staff elected and did it change its structure or was it to all intents and purposes the same composition and structure as the first initial staff?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the first staff was Salih Ruvic, and the second commander was Sabic Muharem, Muharem Sabic. We can say that the structure of the previous staff was maintained, but there was an addition to the new staff. More people were added. I can't tell you of any more -- about this in more detail, but the structure remained the same with new people added on. So the new staff had a new commander and new people.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When did that happen? You didn't tell me when the new staff was established.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this happened after the one-month deadline expired, during which time a joint staff of Prozor municipality was supposed to have been formed after the joint decision that was taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: A month after the 15th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16th of April. It was a day late.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So it had to be later.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you involved in these two bodies in any way? If I understood you correctly, the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people was in fact a political body.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And the Territorial Defence Staff would be a military body, or would you tell me what the Territorial Defence Staff was supposed to do, what its task was.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you tell me what point in time precisely, what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right when you say that the Crisis Staff was supposed to be a political body. The Territorial Staff, as there was no army at the time, it hadn't been established, was to take over part of the defence preparations, bearing in mind the political situation prevailing in the area. So that in addition to the people who had military leanings in that staff, there were also political representatives and eminent people.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was the relationship between the War Presidency, which was supposed to be the legitimate organ at a time when an imminent threat of war was being declared, what was the relationship between the War Presidency and the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people? Was it the War Presidency that elected the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer with precision because it wouldn't be logical, but also under normal circumstances it would not be superfluous for the War Presidency to suggest who should be part of that body in view of their political office or government office, so that's how it should be. The structure of the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people was such that there was a representative of the party, a representative of the governmental organs. In other words, people who had political power in the municipality, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this was a self-appointed body, if I can call it that, to the best of your knowledge? Nobody appointed it, as you say. But you participated. You were invited to participate in that body in late March, early April.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: These may have been political decisions and agreements among the leading parties, because to the best of my knowledge, the same situation prevailed among the Croats and the HDZ representatives. To be quite honest, I never entered into the genesis of this nor did the issue of their legality interest me. I was more interested in the contribution they could make and what had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We are talking now about February, 1992, so please don't speak of two staffs. You say August, early April. We are now talking about the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people in February. The legitimacy and legality is something I am referring to because yesterday you often said these were legitimate organs. Therefore, I am trying by my questions to see whether these actually were legal and legitimate organs, and I will continue putting my questions in connection with the Crisis Staff. There is a TO Crisis Staff and there is also a Crisis Staff of the Muslim people. With respect to mobilisation and the political situation of the Muslim people, the status of the Muslim people, at this time I'm referring to March and April, was yet another institution or organisation established which had similar powers in the domain of preparing the people for what, as you say, you felt was about to happen?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Nozica, you asked me something and you didn't let me reply.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please remind me what it was.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked about the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people and whether it was a self-appointed body. I tried to tell you that I did not delve into the issues of its legitimacy and legality, so please take note of this. Secondly, you used some expressions which I feel were not expressions uttered by me, or if I did, I wish to correct myself. There was a Crisis Staff of the Muslim people, not the Crisis Staff of the Territorial Defence. These were two quite different bodies, so let's clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I know this very well. It may have been a slip. There was a TO staff which you say was established on the 28th of March, 1992, and in early February or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Stop. This is again the situation where both the witness and the lawyer - I should put it the other way around, first the lawyer and the witness - speak the same language, and there's always the same problem: You overlap, and it is terrible for the interpreters. They do their best, and I want to pay homage to their efforts, but it's impossible to give a correct translation on that. So you must both wait some time after the other has finished before you start. This is a difficult exercise in patience and in self-control, but it is necessary because otherwise we cannot really follow. I'm sorry to be so -- such a schoolmaster, but it is really in the interests of everyone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In my cross-examination, I do sometimes have to interrupt the witness and explain something. Thank you for saying what you said. We do have the problem of speaking the same language.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But, Witness, in your examination-in-chief, you gave extensive explanations. In cross-examination you will only answer the questions I'm interested in. If you feel you need to clarify further, you can do so during redirect. So please just answer my question. I would now like to go back to something you said which I think has not entered the record. You said that the Crisis Staff was established in late February or early March. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff of the Muslim people. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Please, I have already put this question but I'll go back to it because you didn't reply. At that time - I'm referring to April and May - was any other political body established in Prozor municipality? Did you participate in any other body which had some sort of authority over the Crisis Staff and the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mrs. Nozica. After the electoral committee of the Party of Democratic Action, on the 20th of June I was elected a member of the Executive Board, and six days later, pursuant to the conclusions reached at that meeting, a Coordination Committee for the Protection of the Interests of the Muslim People was established, and I was its first president. But there is a mistake in what you have said. This body was not superior to any other body. Its only role was to coordinate activities and to search for solutions for a peaceful co-existence and respect for the laws of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't see on the record what day you say this body was established. The 20th of June?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 30th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I have omitted to do something, but I will do it now. If the usher could assist me, I wish to hand these documents to the Prosecution. I intend to refer to them now. Please, could we have on e-court Defence Exhibit 2D 0056. If it is not in e-court, I have prepared a copy for the ELMO, and this seems to be a more practical solution.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 3D 0030, this is also a document of Mr. Praljak's Defence. I have their agreement to refer to this document if my document is not in e-court. The document is dated the 9th of July, 1992, and it is an opinion on information about the work of the Coordinating Committee of the Muslim People. We have here a version. There are minutes here of a meeting of this Coordinating Committee of the Muslim People. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to see the whole document, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: No problem. I'll ask the technicians to scroll down or to place the document on the ELMO. Your signature is on page 2. Could we see page 2. Yes. Here we are. Thank you. Do you recognise the document now?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is this a document which, as you say, is authentic? And, unfortunately, your signature is missing here, but is this a document compiled by you? Can we go back to page 1, and could you take a look at the content of the document so you can affirm whether it's authentic or not. You can keep the front page. Is this a document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you just a while ago whether this Coordinating Committee of the Muslim People had any kind of competence or jurisdiction over the Territorial Defence and over the Crisis Staff. I will read the first sentence here. Please follow and we'll see whether it's correct. "Opinion on the information about work." That's the title. And the text reads as follows: "At its session of the 6th of July, 1992, the Committee for the Coordination of Activities of Implementing the Interests of the Muslim People in Prozor Municipality considered the information on the work of the Territorial Defence Staff over the previous current period. In a broad and comprehensive discussion, the participants agreed in their assessment that the activities of this body in the sense of maintaining the identity of the Muslim people in its competence deserves a high assessment, and it deserves the praise and necessary support." This all happened in July, 1992, and you said that this body was established --

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 30th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. That's important. So this is obviously the first or the second meeting of that body. Can it be concluded from what I have read out that you were evaluating information about the work of the Territorial Defence Staff, as it says here, and can you tell me what your competencies were in relation to the staff? I'm referring to this Coordinating Committee.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The title speaks for itself. I was the coordinator. As an experienced lawyer, Mrs. Nozica, you know more than I do, but I do know something. We are not asking these organs to report to us. They are reporting to their own commands. We are simply seeking information about their work and activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, I asked you quite precisely what your relationship was to the Territorial Defence Staff. Was there any official relationship, whether superior or subordinate? You can answer very briefly, and then we can move on. So what was the relationship of this Coordination and the TO staff? The question is a simple one.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrs. Nozica, however long you ask me this question, I would not react, even if I was right in doing so. At these sessions we invited the commander to attend, we asked him for information, and we conveyed to him our standpoints, asking him to avoid incidents and excesses. If there is further need to explain, then there are some other reasons for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I do have to remind you of the fact that you are duty-bound to answer my questions. And we will now proceed, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mrs. Nozica, I think your question was whether the witness had some organic relation to the Territorial Defence. And this is a question you must answer. What was your personal relation to the Territorial Defence organisation? Were you a member? Were you -- did you have any role there? We are entitled to know this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Not as a member of the Territorial Defence. Only as a political person asking for information and coordinating activities, as part of searching for the best possible solutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even though I don't see how relevant this is as it is part of the cross-examination, but you were asked to establish the connection - legal connection, of course - between this Coordinating Committee for the Muslim People, which is stemmed or was formed out of the -- in the municipality of Prozor. The Prozor municipality is a legal entity, and what has been called Territorial Defence, the Territorial Defence is also a legal entity. So is there a connection between this Coordinating Committee and the Territorial Defence? I think this is what was meant by the question. If there is no connection, were you able to give instructions or orders to the Territorial Defence? I think you have some understanding of legal matters, so you should be able to understand my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. No legal link or connection between the Coordinating Committee and the Territorial Defence Staff, and we weren't able to issue any orders to them, but we were able to convey our opinions and views and requests and demands that they do everything not to make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That was very important for me precisely because of the following question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May we scroll down the document until we get to point (c), which should be the conclusions of this body. That's fine. Thank you. Now, if we look at this document, then under (c) it says: "Our concrete activity would be contained in the following," and then it says to elaborate: "The necessary minimum of weapon supplies and equipment supplies (according to some specifications). The wearing of weapons, maintaining them, using weapons and equipment." Then the third bullet point, not quite clear there, the formation of an information service. The deployment of our units outside or use of our units outside the territory of our municipality. The elaboration of criteria for mobilisation, a completing action, and stating what weapons were procured with people's resources, with the resources belonging to us; forming units for the defence of the town, and the training of recruits, young men. I don't think that we need to be a legal expert to conclude that you did nonetheless deal with questions that come under the military realm, because you say here that you're going to elaborate or give instructions about very concrete action that is to be implemented by the Territorial Defence. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right if you were to look at only one side of the coin.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid I'm not interested in the other side of the coin at present, so let's leave that alone.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But for the purposes of truth we'll have to look at both sides of the medal.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Prosecutor will ask you if he wants to hear.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is all done on assumption --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and make pauses between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, I can very well understand that you feel an urge to point to things which the lawyer does not ask of you, but it is for us to see that the balance is finally established, and at this moment the phase of the proceedings of the trial is a bit unilateral, and I'm afraid that you are obliged to accept this and really just to answer the questions that are put to you. You must have confidence in those who run the trial, which is the Prosecutor mainly, and also in the Bench, that in the end a balance is established. But we do not get along if you constantly try to take this opportunity to state your personal views and to give in to your urge to explain. It is difficult, I know, because I have also been in that situation, but I must ask you to put up with this. It is the rules, and we must abide by the rules. Please continue, Mrs. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As far as I understand, I still have five more minutes. Is that the case? Do I have five more minutes and then I can round off this part of my questioning? Very well. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, we now see that, at the latest, by the 30th of June, as you said, three bodies were set up by the members of the Muslim people; the Crisis Staff of the Defence of the Muslim people, the Territorial Defence Staff, and this Coordinating Committee of the Muslim People. Can you tell me whether you consider -- I'm just interested in hearing your opinion -- that these were legal and legitimately elected organs.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the formation of the coordinating body and Territorial Defence Staff, the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people disappeared, and with the formation of those two bodies, yes, that was considered to be legal and legitimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You also state that the Crisis Staff disappeared. What took over its role?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the political portion, the Executive Board of the party --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Which party?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Party of Democratic Action. Which was elected at the Assembly of the 24th of June. That's when the elections were held. And the Coordinating Board, or committee, took this over, and what was up to the Territorial Defence is what they did. They did -- saw to questions under their realm. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May I conclude, then, that the Party of Democratic Action and this Coordinating Board of the Muslim People took over the political role and the TO staff remained as the military section; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, is that how it was, according to you? Was that legitimate and legal? Does it say anywhere in our rules and regulations -- and let me remind you of what you know and what I know: When Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognised, that that was on the 6th of April, 1992. Before and after that, at any time did political power and authority over the army, was that the coordinating body and political party? Could that have been what -- who was in charge, or in the Republic -- in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and later on in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina that it was a legal organs?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what prevailed before, but I know that was the case here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I said I don't know. I'm asking the witness. I don't know what "there" and "here" means. What does he mean?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I understood you to say that in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the rest of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were cases where there was political control. That's how I understood you. And I claim there was none here, whereas over there, where you had in mind, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're saying. What do you mean by political control? Where? You said a moment ago that the HDZ and the Coordinating Board had political -- I made a mistake, a slip of the tongue, yes, the SDA, had political control over the Territorial Defence. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coordinating role. Not a political role, but a coordinating role.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Coordinating role can be anything; physical labour, singing, whatever. I'm talking about the political role. Was that the coordinating role?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not and it could not have been, and do you know why? Because the Coordinating Board was formed on a very broad basis, on the basis upon which the platform of the Presidency was also established, and in the Coordinating Board you had people from all the other parties, very prominent figures, not only SDA members, and that's a great difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'm in a complete quandary. A moment ago you said that the Crisis Staff replaced -- was replaced by the legally elected representatives of the SDA and Coordinating Board of the Muslims; is that right? Let's move on quicker, otherwise we can go round and round in circles, and then we can move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the work of the Crisis Staff was transferred to these institutions, the ones we're talking about, or these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what about the rest of the business?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nothing else remained. What remains? There's nothing else left.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then your precise answer would be that all the authorisations of the Crisis Staff was passed on to these institutions. You say a part, and then you say there's nothing left, but if there's nothing left, then it's all of them. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people no longer exists, then that would be logical that in the political sense part of the work would be done by the SDA party. What the army should do was done by the Territorial Defence Staff, and what you had to coordinate, that was taken over by the coordinating body, the Coordinating Committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think that it's time to take a break, and I'll continue after we reconvene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 12.30. We're going to take a break for an hour and a half and reconvene at 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. I give the floor to Counsel Nozica once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, before my colleague Ms. Nozica resumes her cross-examination, we did observe just before Your Honours entered that the witness appeared to be referring to some documents. I'm not sure whether these were documents contained in his briefcase or otherwise, but we are concerned, and I would ask Your Honour to make some inquiry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Sir, we've just been told that you were consulting some documents. What are the documents that you have before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The platform for the actions of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- for the activities of Bosnia-Herzegovina in wartime conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that's the document that you were looking at? Do you have any others there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just brought a document that we finished discussing. So I was just brought that document prior to the beginning of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that you were brought it. Who brought it to you? Who handed you the document? Who gave you that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar or the secretary, or I am not quite sure what the official title of the person who gave it to me is. It's the document that I was questioned on. I was asked whether it was an authentic document and whether I had signed it. It's the document we discussed before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to ask that the witness take away all the documents except the document that we've discussing and that was handed to him for the cross-examination, so that we can continue. Thank you. Now, as you're already there, would you show the witness document 2D 0055, Defence document, and it's a report on the work of the staff of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Prozor, the date is the 16th of September, 1992. I don't know whether we have it in e-court, but I think it will be quicker if we place it on the overhead projector.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We have the document before us, and it's on e-court too. Can you recognise the document? Do you recognise it? Whose document is this, judging by the name and date when it was compiled?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date I can see is the 16th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And would you look at the bottom of the document and tell us who signed it. Do you know the person who signed it, and was the person occupying this post that it says they were?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That has nothing to do with our Coordination Board. This was separate.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I didn't say that. May we have the first page again, please, on our screens. Thank you. Before the break we spoke about legality, the legality of both the Crisis Staff and the TO staff. I'm going to read out the first paragraph and please tell me if that's what it says: "The staff of the Territorial Defence of Prozor municipality was formed on the 2nd of April, 1992, by the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people. The staff of the TO of Prozor achieved its legitimacy by the acts and documents of the Main Staff of the armed forces, number 02/507-3, dated the 5th of July, 1992, on the appointment of the commanders or commander of the Municipal Staff of Prozor Defence." And the number is 02/583-1, "dated the 17th of July, 1992, the order on a provisional subordination of the Municipal Staff of Prozor to the District Staff of the Zenica region." Is that what it says in this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. That will suffice. I don't need any more comments from you. We can just observe that, with respect to the date, the TO staff -- the date of the formation of the TO staff is somewhat different here than you said in your testimony and is different from what it says in the information describing the situation in the municipality of Prozor before and after the brutal aggression to which the Prosecution referred. Let's move on. A different area but it's the same document. On page 104 of yesterday's transcript, lines 23 to page 105 up to line 12, you spoke about an HVO attack on the 28th of August, 1992, on part of the town where the more prosperous inhabitants lived, and on that occasion you said that a member of the TO was wounded, and that is what you said: "We did not respond from our side." That means --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat what she just said about an attack and conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was an attack from one side. He was wounded by a bomb or by a bullet.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May we now look at the report that we have in front of us, on page 2. And it is 2D 060021, the translation. And the paragraph begins -- that's fine. Leave it there. Linked to that same event, Mr. Muharem Sabic says something quite different, so we're just going to take note of that. The paragraph begins in this way, it is the fifth paragraph: "Relations with the HVO were not at an enviable level, and this was evidenced in the night between the 27th and 28th of August, 1992, where on the occasion there was a conflict in the town of Prozor in which there were wounded on both sides." The next part is not important. Perhaps for another occasion but not just now. So the commander of the municipal defence staff says that there were wounded on both sides. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And we were never presented with a report of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Your answer was no, you don't know. I'm not going to ask you about who presented you with any reports or information. Thank you. So we agree that the commander of the Municipal Staff of the defence of Prozor was the relevant person to convey information. Would you agree with me on that score?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's not proper if he conveyed different information.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't know who conveyed different information. It's up to the Court to establish that and decide. On page 111, and we are staying with the same document for the time being, lines 11 onwards, lines 11 to 18, you spoke about the number of members of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the TO, or the Municipal Staff of the defence of Prozor, and you said that there was a total of 100 plus or -- well, 150, 100 towards the Chetnik front and 100 to 150 in Prozor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the data that we had at your disposal, that's what I could have said on the basis of that, but we didn't have any more detailed information.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What time are we talking about? When did you have this information and when did you dispose of these figures and data? Yesterday you were saying that within the framework of the context of the events prior to October, 1992. Are we referring to the same period of time?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Let's go back to the first page of this report then, please. And I'm going to read out the portion where it says that: "The Municipal Staff --" second paragraph, first page: "The Municipal Staff of the defence of Prozor has engaged 800 fighters, and these fighters are deployed to perform functions in 10-day-shifts of which 300 fighters are permanently engaged on the Prozor-Kupres battlefront of which 100 fighters are located in joint units with the HVO, the crew operating heavy weapons, howitzers, tanks, mortars, PAMs and PATs, whereas 200 members of our army are located on the front line at the following localities: Idovac-Kik-Kicelj-Kriz-Straza-Rosulje-Zvirnjaca. The fighters are equipped with good artillery and infantry weapons mostly."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Are you sure you have "artillery" in the original version? Because in the translation it does not figure. The word "artillery" does not figure in the translation. I just want to avoid misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "Infantry."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm not sure I used the word. Is that all right now? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So I was referring to machine-guns. AP would be an automatic rifle. Light machine-guns, automatic rifles, then PAP would be a semi-automatic rifle, and RB would be hand grenade. Is that what it says in this report?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't guarantee for the third. It's smudged over the third letter, PAP, P-A-P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry, but I'm looking at the translation, and the translation speaks of rocket launcher, and that would be a bit different from hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] Rocket launcher, RB. RB, rocket launcher. No. I misspoke. [In English] Okay. Sorry. [Interpretation] Hand-held mortar, "rucni bacac," hand-held mortar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, my question related to the number of members of the municipal defence staff of Prozor. So this is a report, not quite a direct one, but several months before the conflict. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, madam, but the way in which you're reading this, you're only looking at it partially, only what suits you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, I'm not looking at the whole text.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't answer what you want to hear. If the president of the Trial Chamber will let me clear this matter up. It needs clarification, perhaps at a different date.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether it says 800 fighters?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you want to question and challenge the number I mentioned, and I spoke about the number of fighters in town whereas this, the number of 800, is fighters from all over town, all over the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We'll get to fighters in town, but you said a total number of men in Prozor, there was a maximum of 250 fighters.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that particular night.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You didn't say on that particular night.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there we go, I'm saying it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, fine, but you didn't say 250 fighters that night initially. That's very interesting, it's interesting for me to note that. But I'm not going to dwell on that now. Let's move on. It goes on to say: "The position at the Kupres-Prozor battlefield were holding together with the HVO from the -- and we have been doing so from the beginning of April, so that we are applying a 10-day schedule -- shift." And then the next sentence begins: "In addition to the above-mentioned, 300 members of the BH army of the Prozor municipality is engaged in securing the Municipal Staff of defence, the communications centre, and the important facilities as well as security for the town itself, for the other village watches, and mostly they have very poor weapons." Now, I don't want to say what the PPS, the MAP 48 - I know what that is, that's a rifle - and a carbine - I know what that is too. Does it say here that 300 members of the Municipal Staff of the defence of Prozor were engaged in the town itself? Is that what it says? So if we add these 300, we're still missing 200 because there are a total of 800. Is that what it says in this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your arithmetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm not doing arithmetic. I'm reading. I'm reading out a piece of information supplied by the commander of the municipal defence staff of Prozor dated the 16th of September, 1992. As we have no reason to doubt the correctness of this data, or maybe we do but you will tell us if the data is incorrect or if you believe it to be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this data has to be clarified with the authors of these reports. I cannot assert that they are correct nor can I accept that they are incorrect, because according to the calculation you're using, you're talking about Prozor and the entire municipality, and from what you read I don't think it's clear. I think it should be clarified with those who wrote these reports, with the authors. This is the first time I've seen this document, so I cannot comment on it in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... in paragraph 2, 800 fighters were mentioned. So we have this figure of 800. Then afterwards he said that there were 300 which are on the Kupres-Prozor line. So 800 minus 300 leaves 500. The text continues. There are 200 who are on the Idovac-Kik-Kicelj-Kriz et cetera, line. So if I subtract the 200, we have 300 left, and I find those 300 in that last paragraph where apparently those 300 were providing security, general security for the OPSO, the communications centre, and so on and so forth. So there you have the figures. Perhaps you have a different vision of the figures. Tell us, please, with respect to this document, what -- are you challenging those figures or not? Because arithmetic is very precise here. We have very clear addition and subtraction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, these 300 fighters linked to the town, that's the number I was referring to. The overall number covering the territory of the entire municipality which went out in shifts, well, they weren't all there at every point in time. They would spend 10 days there and go back, and so on. The 300 refers to the town and to what I was talking about yesterday. Maybe I misunderstood, which is why I said that the arithmetic was not clear to me. But after Your Honour's clarification, I think that's how it could be.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank His Honour, but I will say that I still miss 200, and I'll tell you why. In the first passage it says that 800 were engaged, 300 constantly on the Prozor-Kupres war front. So a hundred are in joint units and 200 in separate units. That's why my view and linguistic interpretation, but that's not so important now.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But what you are saying today is quite different from what you said yesterday. Yesterday you said quite precisely that there were a hundred fighters on the line facing the Chetniks. So this could not be the 250 or 300 we're talking about now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, I would like to intervene. In paragraph 2, 800 are mentioned on the Prozor-Kupres front line, and in English it is specified that amongst those 300, 100 are in joint units together with the HVO. So there are 300 overall on the front line, there are 100 who are side by side with the HVO. Therefore, there are 200 who must be part of the BiH army. That's how we can interpret this. Of course, it could be perceived in another way, or understood in another way.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The purpose of presenting this document was to show -- to show what the total number of fighters was according to the official reports of the Municipal Defence Staff of Prozor at that time. Excuse me, Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you would like this number to be clarified, I can assist. If not, I will sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could you enlighten us as far as the figure goes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 300 men who are together on the front line in one shift are divided into two parts. A hundred men from the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina are together with the HVO as tank crews, artillery crews, and the mortar crews. Two hundred men are holding their own part of the front line, which is precisely designated next to the HVO but not together with them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to thank Mr. Praljak. That's how I understood it too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I would now like to deal with this number of 300 in the town. Tell me, in your experience, what did this line with the Chetniks look like at the time? Was there any serious possibilities that the Chetniks might break through or conduct shelling? I see that you were engaged not only as a politician but also in military terms. So how dangerous was it or what was the threat that the line might be fall and what was the threat to Prozor?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course you'd have to ask military experts about this, but as far as I know, the distance was such that the threat was not a great one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I will show you on page 2 of this same document what a professional person thought about this, the Staff Commander, that is. That's the first paragraph on page 2 or in the translation 2D 060211: "The Defence line on the Prozor-Kupres war front is not an innocuous one and is strategically very important. The Chetnik infantry is attempting to pierce through the defence line especially on the Idovac elevation 1.156 metres from where they would have the possibility of firing from howitzers." Is that what it says in this report?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it said in the report at the time, but this was so far from the town of Prozor that I don't believe that even had the line fallen, the town would not have been under threat because new lines would have been taken up. And to the best of our knowledge, their forces were not sufficient to threaten the town of Prozor itself. But as I said, such military assessments, especially without preparation, is something I would ask you to ask me as little about as possible, because I don't --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, my time is very limited, and I would not have asked you anything had you said that you knew nothing about it. But as you yourself embarked on an assessment, saying that this was not a threat to Prozor, that's why I went further into this question. If you don't want me to go into a question any further, tell me that you don't know or that it's beyond your experience. We'll come to the issue of distance and how far this was from Prozor. The reason I'm asking you all this is you, I put it to you, were involved in the Crisis Staff and in all these events as part of your coordinating activities and analysing the activities of the TO staff, so please tell me, why was there a need to have 300 fighters in the town? Can you say anything about this from your own experience?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to the need for such a large number, I have no experience or knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. I will refer to the report which states why this is happening. In paragraph 2, which speaks of the number of men in town, it says: "We are doing this for reasons of prevention." I will now move on to another topic. Yesterday, on page 97 of the transcript, from 9 to 24, you spoke about the unequal relationship between the members of the Bosniak nationality and the HVO, and I'm referring now to the joint lines. You spoke about some 20 Bosniaks who were left without weapons. I would now like to go back to this report. We needn't look at it again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. Ms. Nozica, you have quoted, I read, paragraph -- on line 7, page 82. "In paragraph 2, which speaks of the number of men in town, it says: 'We are doing this for reasons of prevention.'" I was trying to find this paragraph and could not. Perhaps you could indicate more precisely where the quotation is to be found. I would not like you to stay in an area of doubt there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you're looking on page 7 or 82, you will not find it. I said 97. But I will have a look at the transcript now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may assist. If I could direct the attention to the final sentence of the fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Oh. "For preventive measures." Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I'm a bit confused now. I was referring to the transcript of yesterday. I would like to thank my learned friend for assisting me. Now I will come back to this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said that the relationship was not on a footing of equality. Do you abide by that statement now? Because we have information from Mr. Sabic, who is saying that the 200 members of our army who are on the front line, they are equipped with artillery weapons, automatic and semi-automatic rifles, infantry weapons, and a hand-held rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, allow me to reply by reading the text of the document which clearly confirms what I said, but Mrs. Nozica is skilfully taking only what suits her. [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot interpret when speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] This is all in the document. Why are you skipping over it? It's describing the situation and the equality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, you are right. It describes precisely the situation of the members of the municipal TO staff of Prozor municipality. I was not going to skip over it. It talks about the attitude of the municipal TO staff towards its members. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to my question. You cannot answer my questions with a question. At least, I think that's not permissible in these proceedings. Please tell me, these 200 members who held the line independently on their own, as Mr. Praljak explained, were they well-armed, according to this information? Do you challenge this information?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can neither challenge nor confirm it. I can only suggest that this should be checked with the people who are competent to answer and who are the authors of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, can we then take it that your testimony contradicts the document signed by Commander Muharem Sabic?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would not say that it completely contradicts. It's partly different with regard to the figures relating to the Prozor municipality and Prozor and the numbers of men holding the front lines in shifts. I was not fully informed of that, and it's not important. These are just nuances.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You may consider that these are just nuances, but here it says, referring to the town of Prozor, they are armed with poor weapons, not not armed at all. These are semi-automatic rifles, carbines, and rifles which I agree are not very good ones, but this is something quite different. I will now move on to another topic so as to leave time for Mr. Kovacic. On page 115 of yesterday's transcript, you spoke about the weapons that the HVO it. Is that correct? And you said, I will quote you, when asked by His Honour, you responded by saying that the Croatian side could not have had heavy weapons or tanks, armoured personnel carriers, and heavy weapons. Is this correct? Did you say that the HVO could not have had - that's what it says - tanks, armoured personnel carriers? And the date we are talking about is the 23rd of October. That's the date you designated as the date of the attack on Prozor. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly not in those quantities.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What quantities? Now you're adding quantities. You didn't mention that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. If there was a blockade of all roads approaching the town, if in front of the police station there were personnel carriers, if there was that number of tanks deployed --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How could you have seen all those from a basement?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I felt this, and I told you personally that I saw two tanks firing when I was pulling out on Saturday morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Hujdur. There was a long debate in which the Bench got involved yesterday as to who it was who participated in the fighting around Prozor. There was a long debate, and your purpose was to show that there were members of the HV, the Croatian army, present there. When asked very specifically by Judge Antonetti who you were referring to when you said the Croatian army, you replied, "I'm referring to those who participated in the attack. The HVO could not have had tanks, armoured personnel carriers, and heavy weapons." Did you say that or not? It's very simple: Did you say that yesterday or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you have pulled the question out of context.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, then, please explain the context. I'll tell you let me what the context is. Did it have these weapons and then not have them?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they couldn't have had weapons in those quantities for that amount of firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, that's completely different from what you said yesterday. I'll come back to this information. This is a report on the work of the Municipal Staff of Prozor. We read out this part several times. I'm going to read it out again: "100 fighters -- 100 fighters are found in joint units with the HVO crews on heavy weapons, howitzers, tanks, mortars, and PAM and PATs; is that right? Did you know about that? Did you know that the HVO had this kind of weaponry at the time at the Prozor-Kupres battlefront? I'm not going to ask you what they had in Prozor, but did you know about this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, as far as the mortars are concerned. As to the rest, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. We can agree, then, that you misspoke yesterday when you said the HVO did not have these weapons, that you spoke wrongly, and now you're putting yourself right; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. APC -- the APC that I personally saw in front of the police station was quite certainly not at the front line. Neither that one nor others.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's an enormous APC. It's terrible to look at. It had to use proper roads not go up to the front line along the hills.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you just tell me how you come to know that? How could you know that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, do you have to have any special knowledge? When you see this enormous beast of an APC, you know that it can't go up a mountain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've just said that there was this enormous APC, and you saw it with your very own eyes, did you, this enormous vehicle? And in general, the APCs have names, there are signs on it, insignia. Did you see anything, any markings, as far as you remember, on the APC, on this armoured vehicle, or did it just have one colour without any special markings? Do you remember having seen any markings on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I personally saw the APC in front of the police station, but out of fear I just wasn't able to notice any markings on it, whether it had any or didn't. And that same APC I saw that night, too, around midnight. It was in the lower part of town by a bridge where it managed to turn round, but it's a terrible vehicle. Looks absolutely frightening. I don't have the time or the space to describe just how dreadful and fear inspiring this vehicle looked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And were there any cannons on -- guns on this APC, any crew, any turret, or anything like that, antennae of any kind, satellite antennae or anything like that? Do you recall seeing anything like that on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as to barrels or guns and antennae, I did see some, and some small openings, but I really can't remember all the details. Some small openings on the armoured part of the APC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague was just -- I asked whether there were any tracked, traction or wheels, or was it a tracked vehicle? Because when a tracked vehicle turns, when it's caterpillar-type vehicle, then it makes a noise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the best will in the world, I'm afraid I can't say whether I noticed any of those details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Counsel Nozica, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, as His Honour asked you, you didn't see any licence plates or anything like that, so you still can't say whether this vehicle belonged to the HVO or to someone else. That would be correct, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I still say that it could not have been an HVO vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So your doubts and suspicions is one thing, but concrete -- something concrete is different. I have every reason to suspect that it was HVO, but I'm asking you again: Can you tell me whether this specific vehicle belonged to the HVO or to the Croatian army, as you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still think that it was owned by the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. It's your right to think that, but let's move on and deal with the meeting of the 23rd of October, 1992. Yesterday in your testimony, you said that at one point in time Ilija Petrovic came by and said, "While we're talking, you balijas, you're killing our people. There can be no discussion with you. You have to surrender your weapons within five minutes." And he said that on that day you received information according to which a member of the HVO was killed during the meeting, and you said that you used radio communication to check this out and that nobody had been killed that day but that two or three days earlier on, in Gornji Vakuf, a member of the HVO had been killed. And then you said that all that -- that was all they had -- that everything that they had done had been stage managed. I thought that the next document was in e-court, 2D 00054. I don't know whether it is in e-court. There's -- there's some problems, but ... Can you tell us what this is about? What document is this? Can you tell me before I tell you?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a certification of death.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: A death certificate for Zadro Franjo; is that right? And is that the fighter that they said was killed on that day, the 23rd of October, when Ilija Petrovic entered the meeting? Did he mention this name?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you ever learn that that soldier who was killed was -- was called like that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you take a look at where this person was killed and when. Was he killed on the 23rd of October, 1992, at 1300 hours? Is that what it says on this document? Let me just ask you, is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that should be checked out.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The person who should check this out will no doubt do so, but if you doubt the authenticity, that's your affair. If the Prosecutor wants me to prove it, then I will prove that the document is authentic. May we scroll down to look at the bottom of the document and see if there's a stamp and who issued it. Yes, it has a stamp. It says in Prozor, the 16th of June, 2006. The number is 41/2006. So it's very easy to check the authenticity of the document. Fine, we can scroll up again now, thank you. Just a minute, please. What does it say about this person? Where was this person killed? Where did they die?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date of issuance is not the right one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Never mind. If you have any problems with this document -- just answer my questions. If you doubt the authenticity of the document, I can prove -- I have ways of proving that this is indeed an authentic, original document, but tell me where this person died.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says Crni Vrh, but that's not Prozor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is it territory towards Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it might be over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is then that the story that you told us yesterday that this could be the individual who you said that three days earlier, before the 23rd, had been killed somewhere towards Gornji Vakuf and that this was used by the HVO to leave the meeting and to launch the attack on the town, as you said?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. That's the information that we had, and all that needs to be checked out, as does what it says in this document, with all due respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, how were you able to check whether anybody had been killed?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the TO staff we used our communication lines to check out all the lines and front lines and to see whether that was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You used analytical work. You gathered information. I'm sure you wanted to establish the truth that was important for the Muslim people and all other peoples. After this event, at any time after this event -- you seem to be accusing the HVO of making use of this, of making false use of this to launch an attack. Did you ever check to see whether actually -- whether somebody was actually killed on that day, whether this person was actually killed? Did you ever take the trouble to check that out later on?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: After official information from the TO that this was not true and that it had happened several days before on the territory of another municipality, we didn't check it out because we thought that that was the truth. Of course we would like to establish the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If this document is correct and you're challenging its authenticity, whereas I tell you that it is authentic, so if this is indeed from a death certificate, does it change your opinion as to how the conflicts began between the HVO and the TO on that particular day? Do you still maintain what you said, that they left the meeting because something incorrect, a false event had been used as a pretext to leave the meeting and start the attack? Does it change your opinion had you known about this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but everything had to be checked out first.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So do I, but that was your duty. It was your duty to --

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, come on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and speak one by one, with pauses in between. It's impossible to translate at this rate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your information on the 12th of March, 1993 - and it is P 01656, that's the number of the document - in that information you describe this event and accuse the HVO of presenting incorrect data. I do not say that it is your fault, but you should have checked out that information. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let us agree to disagree.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We should have checked it altogether.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was checked.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, come on. If it happened at 1300 hours, how could it have been checked out?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. The person who informed you about this at the meeting informed you of an event that actually happened. Now, let's move on. I said that I didn't expect you to agree with me but I have to indicate the following, although I'm convinced that the Trial Chamber will bear that in mind: In the information that I referred to earlier on of the 12th of March, 1993, and it is Prosecution Exhibit P 01656, page 9, you describe this event. It is the Bosnian version, and the translation is on page 10. You didn't say that anybody said "balija, five minutes," that bit. You didn't mention that. Do you remember that better today or when you compiled the information? Let me read out what you said. "During the break, the president of the HDZ of Prozor, Ilija Petrovic, in a very brusque way told us that, 'While you're negotiating with us, you're killing our people,' and all the members of the Croatian delegation left the premises of the negotiations." Is it true that he said balija and so on, the five minutes and balija?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But you didn't remember that when you were writing, compiling this information or report. I just have two very brief questions to ask you. Yesterday, you spoke about the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you said that the beginning of the conflict was April and March, 1992. Am I right? We're talking about the Serbo-Chetnik or Serbian aggression or JNA aggression, or whichever terminology you like to use.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in that context, that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you hear that in 1991, for instance, in May, there was an attack on the village of Unista, a Croatian village, in 1991, that it was attacked by the JNA? Did you hear about those events?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the Ravno area?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll come to Ravno. Let me ask you about Ravno straight away, then. Did you hear of Ravno having been attacked in September, 1991? This is all Bosnia-Herzegovina we're talking about now.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you should ask somebody else that question. I can't claim --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness. Witness. I'm sorry. You are really being extremely undisciplined. I have told you clearly that you have to answer the question and it is not for you to tell the Defence counsel or anybody in this room who they must put a question to. If a question is put to you, you have to answer it, full stop. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked this because you said that the aggression began in March and April, 1992. That's why I'm asking you whether you heard about the attacks on the villages of Ravna, Unista, about the arrival of the JNA in Mostar, and the incidents in Bijeljina, which all took place before March and April, 1992. Have you heard about this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I heard about the village of Unista which you mentioned was today. As for Ravno, I heard about this, that it happened in September. But when I spoke about the aggression, I was referring to large-scale or open aggression to the definition as defined.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to Your Honours. I was trying to say that I was not a person who can answer such a question, and it was in this context I wanted to answer. I'm not trying to be undisciplined. There can only be a misunderstanding or a different understanding, so please take that into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This information presented to you by the Prosecutor -- can we have the Prosecution document P 01656 put on e-court. P 01656, the last page, where the signatures are. Although we don't see the signatures, we do have the names and titles of the persons. Does it say here that Salih Ruvic is the commander of the Municipal Defence Staff of Prozor, and did he hold that post at the time he signed this information? The information was compiled, let me remind you, on the 12th of March. Today you told me he held that post only very briefly and that he was replaced by Mr. Saric. Was he holding that post at this time?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the fall of Prozor, he was again commander in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So in Jablanica he was the staff commander elected later on. When was this staff appointed?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it has to do with the free area of Scipe, Kute, Here, after the fall of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's a temporary territory?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not temporary.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Dislocated territory? Were you or not in Jablanica municipality -- or, rather, in Prozor municipality, is that correct, when you were compiling this information?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not how it was, because we did have communication with that territory, and we went here and there. From Jablanica to that territory, and from that territory to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well, thank you, you explained that today.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one point of clarification regarding this last document. We can see three names; yours, Ruvic, and the president of the SDA. Ahmo Hujdur, is he one of your relatives? What connection is there? Is he your brother or your father? Is he one of your relatives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's just the same last name, but he's even from a neighbouring village, not the same village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for having clarified this. Mr. Kovacic, we have half an hour before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I have already said, please give my client the floor first. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you may ask technical questions, and please put your questions in a calm fashion.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Hujdur. In your statement, you said that I had some connection with Prozor because my father had worked there and I had spent part of my childhood there. I'll ask you directly and please answer me quickly so that my brief questioning can be finished soon. Whether my father was the chief of the police service and the secret service there.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that, but I'm not sure about the details.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: He -- I lived there for four years. Is it well known that I was a relatively good friend of Mr. Hajrudin Rizvanbegovic, the veterinary surgeon there at the time? Yes or no. Say no if you don't know, and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
