utterances.text: Yes, let it be so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Just say you don't know and we can move on.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: When I arrived in Rama at the time you are referring to, was I wearing a camouflage uniform at the meeting you mention?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you were.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. And the insignia on this uniform, were they HVO insignia or HV insignia?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: When I arrived, did I introduce myself, and did I say that I had been asked to come quickly to Rama from Zagreb to calm down an incident where -- by two men, Mr. Franjo Tudjman, the president of the Croatian state, and Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, the president of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Did I introduce myself as such?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You may have introduced yourself in this way but I don't recall that detail.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that before that I had had a meeting in Jablanica, another meeting in Jablanica with Mr. Pasalic and others, followed by a meeting in Konjic, followed by a meeting with 150 Croats from the villages of Rama? Are you aware of all this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know that on that day you arrived in Konjic when we went to Prozor together and met in Jablanica. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You told Their Honours that you wouldn't speak about the curses you heard from me. I don't mind your testifying that I was swearing and cursing.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to talk about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: That I was sometimes very angry; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You have seen me pull out a pistol and point it at people?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, did you hear that I slapped some people? Have you at least heard about that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. That completes this part of my questioning. Just a purely mathematical matter: You said that in Rama there were 3.655 inhabitants. Then you said that two-thirds of that number, or 2.436, were Muslims, Bosniaks. Please, how many people from Rama were Croats -- or, rather, how many Croats and Muslims had left Rama at the time to go and work as migrant workers in France, Germany, Austria and other places? Can we say that at that point in time there were fewer people in Rama than shown by the census?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, just one correction: You're talking about Rama but it's actually Prozor, the seat of the municipality, which still bears the name of Prozor. When I was giving this information, I was talking about the last census. What you say may have been true. There certainly may have been changes, which it is difficult to confirm or deny right now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I'm only trying to say that out of 2.000 Muslim Bosniaks in a place called Rama by the Croats and Prozor by the Bosniaks, there were 2.000, and in the nature of things a thousand would have been men and a thousand women. Out of a thousand men, 200 at least would be children. In mathematical terms, this would mean that on the 23rd most probably in Rama there were approximately 800 men, more or less. These 800 grown men, according to you, were attacked by 2.000 HVO troops and 6.000 outsiders, which would be a total of 8.000 armed soldiers, with tanks, heavy artillery weapons, and a whole arsenal of weapons, and they would have been attacking 800 civilian Bosniaks in a town, and the fighting went on from 1525 hours on one day until noon the following day. And now at the end, the people whom fate has led into war, after all this has occurred, it says that the HVO had five killed, you say that the Muslims or the Bosniaks had 10 killed, and there were 18 wounded. Those are the figures put forward here. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could you just let him answer the question and then we'll hear your objection. Mr. Praljak has just demonstrated mathematically how many people were there, 800 according to his calculation, 800 grown men who could carry weapons. According to him, they would have attacked the 2.000 people from the HVO in addition to the 6.000 outsiders, in other words those people who would have come from outside. By and large 800 people would have attacked 800 soldiers -- 8.000 soldiers, heavily armed, equipped with weapons and tanks. What do you say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen, I do have a lot to say. I'll try and compress it into five minutes. First of all, the name Prozor is still the name of the town. The name of the municipality, Prozor-Rama, is a dual name according to a decision by the arbiter. The figures put forward by General Praljak as to the composition of the population --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but my question doesn't really relate to Prozor. This is what has been put forward by Mr. Praljak to indicate how many men were on either side. So I think there is an idea behind this. I don't know whether you agree or disagree. We'd like to know, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, but Mr. Praljak spoke about the name again, so I wanted to further clarify it. As for the figures, that is a changeable category. Mr. Praljak has the advantage here, because he was in possession of this whole situation. And unfortunately, I cannot agree here. I cannot accept this. I deny it for the following reasons, inter alia: Of the 10 who were killed as registered by the Bosniak side, not a single soldier of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was killed in Prozor. They were all civilians. The only soldier who was killed was killed while pulling out in a place, I think it's called Kranjcici, when he ran into a unit that was there. But in the town of Prozor itself civilians were killed after the shelling stopped. This is not an equal fight. And the commanders who led the attack should discuss the relative strength of the forces, those who led the attack and those who led the defence, if there was any. So I disagree with the general here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kruger, I think you had stood up to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My objection was just to the length of the question which made it very difficult for the witness, and I think for the Court, to identify. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Last question, Mr. Praljak, because your lawyer would also like to say a few things. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: As the lawyers say, for the record, the information I put forward was not any information of mine. I was simply using the information supplied by you, Mr. Hujdur, during your testimony, and I did not say that soldiers were killed. I was just saying that this was the terrible mathematics of death using the figures you gave. I did not provide any figures here. I was only doing the maths. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Kovacic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hujdur, my name is Bozidar Kovacic. I am counsel for General Praljak, and in view of my previous experience, after the cross-examination by my colleague Mrs. Nozica and by General Praljak, I'm simply asking you to show a will to cooperate with this Court. First of all, we speak the same language, so I would like to ask you, even though you understand my question, please wait until you hear in your headset that the interpretation is finished. Otherwise, the interpreters will say they can't hear us. You will understand that there are interpreters sitting behind us who cannot interpret what we say if we both speak at the same time. Therefore, please make a short break after I put my question and I will make a short break after I hear your reply. The problem is simply that we speak the same language, so please bear this in mind. Secondly, I will try to put questions to you which you will be able to answer with a "yes" or "no" or "I don't know," and we can move on. I hope that in this way we will be expeditious. Let's just clarify a few minor facts. First, from your testimony it follows that, inter alia, the inhabitants of your municipality who were liable for military service regardless of the flag under which they served went to certain positions which were held by both Muslims and Croats, and these men came not only from Prozor municipality but other municipalities as well. Is this correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's both correct and not correct. Kuper, near Travnik, I don't think that has anything to do with this. There's only Kupres facing Kupres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. I may have been confused about the positions I was mentioning, but it's a hill overlooking Travnik. Well, then, tell me, what lines against the Serbs did you go to? Kupres? Anything else?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Only Kupres?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, together with the details mentioned just a while ago, a few elevations were there, not to repeat them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you went to that theatre. Both the Croats and the Muslims from Prozor went in a disciplined manner in shifts to hold that front line?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Over a certain time period, but whether in a disciplined manner, one could question that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. The weapons for those men who went to the lines, were they provided by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that most of this was held by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at the overall volume, one might say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. Would you agree with me -- no. I have to reformulate. Not to weary the Court, the Territorial Defence, from the very beginning of the war, before the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina declared independence, already had had its depots emptied. The former JNA -- well, at that time it was still the JNA, together with other federal and Republican institutions simply emptied the depots of the Territorial Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and those weapons were taken to Ljuta near Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the result was the municipal staffs of the Territorial Defence unfortunately were left without any weapons which they had been purchasing many years before the war in the different municipalities; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't deny that, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was the TO capable in 1992 of arming its army? Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it did when it took the weapons from Ljuta near Konjic, which was jointly distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So the source of weapons for the TO was what they managed to seize themselves. That was one source. And the second source of the weapons that belonged to the TO was from the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: What, then?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons from the Ljuta warehouse was equally distributed. It wasn't the weapons from Ljuta that were only given to the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that wasn't sufficient for all the requirements and needs of the next few months. It only covered part of the needs and requirements; is that right? "Yes," "no," or "I don't know." There's no other answer.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim that that was how it was, that there was sufficient quantities or not sufficient. That would be too much to ask of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, yesterday during your testimony, on page 106, around about lines 15 and 16, you mentioned that on the 19th of October - of course we're talking about 1992 - according to your information that there was a conflict between the HVO and the BH army in Novi Travnik, and then you went on to say that as of that day onwards, the number of soldiers in Prozor increased. Since you're not saying which army, is it true that the soldiers on both sides increased, both of the armija and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the increase is concerned -- well, no, not for the armija, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you can't say for certain?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say that somebody came from outside to help the Territorial Defence. So in that sense I can't claim that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Were additional men mobilised?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Is it true and correct, and this would emerge from your testimony although I don't think it wasn't specifically and clearly stated anywhere, whether it would be correct to conclude that the tensions between the Bosnian Croats and Bosnian Muslims in Prozor grew and began to burgeon as of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So those tensions began increasing somewhat earlier, did they not?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But despite that fact, it is a fact that there wasn't a direct conflict between those two sides right up in the events of the 23rd of October. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could be right if you don't skip over the 28th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this conflict on the 28th of August can be considered an incident? That's my first point. And my second point is that all the political players, if I can use that term, and military players, used their goodwill -- demonstrated goodwill to quell the conflict or, rather, not to have a conflict take place and to deal with the damages?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In other words, do you agree that had there not been goodwill on both sides, matters would have been much worse?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would be a logical conclusion that that could have been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you took part in those political negotiations and agreements. Is it true that you all tried to prevent situations of incident -- where incidents took place?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: After this conflict of the 28th of October, which was more serious, judging by its intensity, did not both sides invest efforts to deal with the situation and to try and preserve peace for a certain amount of time?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And with respect to preserving that peace, you mentioned the meeting attended by General Praljak, did you not? Is it true and correct that quite obviously the object of that meeting was to calm the situation and to show people on both sides that they should avoid any conflict which could only work to the advantage of a joint enemy, the VS, Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That might be a strange answer, but if the president will allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had that been the case, then we wouldn't have had all the ultimatums for the disarming of the other villages around the town of Prozor, but these ultimatums continue despite those negotiations, and what happened at the meeting really did happen. That is how matters evolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The incidents to disarm the people didn't happen when my client was there, and the ultimatums.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that day but straight afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. But the fact remains, does it not, that my client insisted and spoke to representatives of both of sides that they preserve the peace, maintain the peace? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he promised a meeting which never came about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I am putting it to you that it wasn't my client who promised to come to the meeting himself. What he said was that the representatives of both sides should maintain regular contacts and meetings, not only in Prozor but further afield as well in order to maintain the peace. He didn't say that he would attend those meetings personally.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But a man of his experience could have concluded that no meetings of that kind would ever take place. So nobody ever understood it that these meetings would not be attended by him or similar figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall we take a break, a 20-minute break, and we will reconvene at ten minutes to four. And we have to finish by 5.15, so as far as possible, the Defence should complete its cross-examination at 5.15. Otherwise, we're going to have to recall the witness in order to continue tomorrow. Mr. Mundis, did you wish to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I believe that, in light of what you've just said, confirms the reason why I went to my feet. I was simply rising to inquire whether we could release the next witness, who's been on standby. It's clear we are not going to get to that witness today, so we would respectfully ask that we can release that witness for today so that he's no longer simply waiting here to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We should tell the witness about tomorrow morning, 9.00. So we reconvene exactly in 20 minutes' time, not 21 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Kovacic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, you recounted your vision yesterday of the situation at the beginning of the conflict on the 23rd of October, 1992, in Prozor. I put it to you that you did not describe the situation correctly or, rather, that maybe you didn't have all the information about the actual state of affairs. And I'm now going to show you a few information -- a few pieces of information and documents so that we can see what it's all about. First of all, on the 21st of October, 1992, already then according to the information that I have, Prozor was asking for assistance to bring the units up to strength from the neighbouring villages. The HVO had taken the town of Makljen, that there was tension in town, and Jablanica sent a company to the borders of Prozor. All the other forces were placed on full combat alert. That same document says that around 1600 hours, Foroz [phoen] said that military police unit and vehicle was left to pass through Prozor with the intention of going on to Travnik. At 1620 hours in Vakuf, the order was to stop them and send them back where they came from, and so on and so forth. So already on the 21st of October, according to this document, Tactical Group 1 Konjic, it would appear that preparations were underway for some sort of activity. Is it true that the Territorial Defence or, rather, the BH army in Prozor was ready for military action and a conflict with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Fine.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nor did it prepare for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask the usher to have a document placed on the ELMO for the witness. Your Honours, we're going to place it on the overhead projector. We don't have a translation because we managed to locate it late last night. It's a short one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the document, please. As we can see, it's a document of the Territorial Defence Staff. Unfortunately, we don't have an English translation. Perhaps the best thing would be for me to read it out. We can see that it is the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the top, Prozor municipality, the Territorial Defence Staff. The number of the document and date are stated. The date isn't clear enough, but it would the 1st of September, 1992. The introductory sentence is the standard one: On the basis of the plan of work as well as on the basis of available MTS - that's the usual abbreviation for materiel and technical equipment - the unit full strength and with respect to an assessment of the political and security situation on the territory of the Prozor municipality and in the Republic, the Prozor TO staff brings in the following plan for the defence of Prozor municipality. Then we have the different elements of that plan. The name of the plan comes first, the location of the mobilisation of the formation, the type of formation planned, the actual numbers in manpower, the place of action, locations, the commander of the unit. And then after that it goes on to explain the plan for the defence of Prozor municipality, because of the situation along the border belt of the Prozor and Kupres municipalities, as well as the situation within the municipality of Prozor itself, has two initial variants. And that's what we're interested in. And it says: "The first is the ELIF plan, which is applied in joint action with the units-formations of the HVO, according to the attached document Alpha. The second variant is plan B, which is applied independently or in joint operation with the TO units of the neighbouring municipalities," and in brackets, it says Gornji Vakuf, Konjic, Jablanica, "according to the attached document Beta." Then we have two attached documents, one, in the title, says -- may we see the top of the document? Yes, top of the document. Further up. Yes. This document is titled document Alfa. We've just mentioned that. And the next attachment is document Beta, as it says at the top of the document. I don't think we need enter into the details of those two documents, document Alfa and document Beta, but my next question is this: Have you had a chance to look through the document, Witness? I claim that from the plan signed by the commander, Muharem Sabic - and you mentioned him several times today - that from that document it clearly emerges that the Territorial Defence from the Municipal Staff of Prozor has developed variants in advance in the sense of two plans. One plan where they are going to work together with the HVO, and plan B was the plan to be applied independently and autonomously, either Prozor or jointly with units from other municipalities; Vakuf, Konjic, Jablanica. Now, do you agree that that document does not -- show that the Territorial Defence on the 1st of September, already on the 1st of September has its plan for every situation; a variant on its own independently or with the HVO against the Serbs. Do you agree that that would be the conclusion on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, you cannot comment. Now, the next document I'd like to show you is in e-court. Madam Usher, [In English] I don't think you will be -- yes. Thank you. [Interpretation] This is our document 3D 00284 or 3D 11004.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting for the document to appear on the e-court system, if I may just indicate that the Prosecution has not received any copies of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm really sorry. I thought we gave them the copy. But haven't you got the entire folder? This one. If you would be so kind, you will get it. And this one, because I don't think this one is in the folder. I don't think that this one is in the folder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: I thank my learned friend, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I really apologise. I was convinced that we gave it to you. [Interpretation] In any case, all the further documents are in e-court, so there should be no further problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, I hope you've had a chance to see the document which is now on the screen. This is a document by the security and information service of the HVO in Prozor, dated the 7th of October, 1992. It was compiled and signed by the chief of security in the brigade, Luka Markesic. Here he makes a request of the brigade in order to have some problems solved, and he refers to a person called Rasim Pilav. Is this name familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that he was a violent man? In fact, there were two brothers that had a group of their own and that they caused quite a lot of damage, to use the most neutral term, and that they were active both within the Territorial Defence and independently. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm seeing this for the first time, so I can't comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. But you must have heard of this person, Rasim Pilav.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And would you agree that he was a certain force to be reckoned with, that he had a group of his own and that he acted not only within the TO but also on his own initiative? You're not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Really, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This intelligence officer, in the paragraph before the last, says that: "Bearing in mind that he -" this man Pilav - "has a lot of weapons and equipment and also a large group of people who are preparing only for conflicts with the Croats and no measures are being taken against him by the civilian and military police police, we feel that certain action has to be taken urgently to suppress his activity." Have you heard of any efforts to arrest him or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this detail, but let me say a few words about this man. He was the owner of a catering establishment which was halfway between Prozor and Jablanica. When you visited the area, you may have seen that building, which was very badly damaged, razed to the ground and hasn't been rebuilt yet. As an individual, he couldn't have done all this or had a large group of men. So this is the first time I've heard of anything like this. And I don't know, I'm not aware of our having been informed of any incident caused by him. I'm not trying to deny that there may have been incidents of that kind, but the police was a joint police, and it would have been better if they had worked together. I'm not saying this is not the case, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's leave that for the present. This person is mentioned again in other documents. But what matters now is that you have heard of him. I will now ask for the next document, 3D 0046 or 3D 030049. While we are waiting for this document, I will only briefly mention what this document is. The author of the document is the same. It's on the screen now. It was issued on the 16th of October. This is a report on current events on the territory of the municipality, and a lot of observations are mentioned, including an introductory sentence which reads as follows: "On the occasion of the complete division between the HVO and the TO, especially with respect to logistics and the military police, there has been a brief lull in the activity of extremist individuals who are probably taken aback by the problems they're facing after this division." My question to you is the following: Are you aware that the HVO and the TO divided or -- their military police and logistics in October?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were informed at the coordination bodies, we were told that logistics was first denied to the army. After that, there was a division, and after that the military police was divided as well. We were informed about this, but as for the details, we didn't know any more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. A few statements are made. First of all, that on the 5th of October, 1992, incidents started that the military police from Jablanica, Safet Indic, known as Bozo, took the main elevation above the village of Toscanica. Do you know this person Safet Indic, a military policeman from Jablanica? That's the military police of Bosnia and Herzegovina, of course, as you can tell by the person's name.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him personally, but I have heard of this nickname Bozo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether on the 3rd of October, 1992, he and his men took an elevation overlooking the village of Toscanica?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of October -- well, that's an incident we need not go into, but then the author goes on, the sentence before the last on this page in the Croatian text, "In the Rama organisation --" this seems to be an abbreviation for an enterprise -- "one of the most important facilities, currently everything is in the hands of members of the Muslim nationality." So this means that a facility is in the hands of the BH army. And several more incidents are described, but no special reference is made to BH army positions. Have you heard of any of these incidents?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I think it's not true that some facilities, because I worked in the Rama hydroelectric power plant for 15 years and I know each facility in detail. Neither at the dam nor in the power plant or anywhere else were only Muslims employed. So this information is certainly incorrect. I worked in that company and I can assert that this is completely untrue. I can't talk about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: A question. On page 2 in this document it says that on the 15th of October, 1992, there were incidents in the villages of Huducko and Toscanica. Do you remember that, the 15th of October? Quite a lot has been said about this, and I know about it from some other information. Does this jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately, I'm not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The next document is 3D 00285, or for the Court, 3D 11007. This is a request. Yes, that's the document. The author again is the chief of security of the brigade, and he makes a request from the brigade command to urgently establish an intervention unit with its headquarters in the town and to find accommodation for that unit and to have it on the alert constantly. And he explains this by saying that: "Bearing in mind the current situation as well as the tense relations between the HVO and the Municipal Staff of the BH and the possibilities of incidents between them, we must have a unit which will be able to intervene at any point in time. This unit should have as its members mature and serious soldiers and they should be trained properly and equipped with the necessary equipment and materiel. Please deal with this problem in the most serious manner and as soon as possible." Based on this information, I feel that -- or I believe that relations were complex at the time, and this person is proposing that a special unit be established in order to maintain order. It follows from this that there must have been a reason for such a request. Were there any incidents caused by members of both sides?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the last part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in the course of October there were incidents, regardless of which side initiated them?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in our previous responses we did say that in this period the logistics were separated, the military police were separated, and all this took place without any incident until the flag was taken down. As for this period, I don't recall, and nobody informed us of any such thing. As for this document, it was addressed to the HVO command at a time when in Prozor one could already feel troops and equipment being concentrated. On that day this letter was written and maybe this man had good intentions when he wrote this if he didn't know what the purpose of the increase of the numbers of troops and equipment in Prozor was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask for the next document, 3D 00287, or 3D 110011 for the Court. While we are waiting for this document to come up on the screen -- here it is. This is what you were mentioning. The same person, the chief of security, the man who is tasked with collecting information and forwarding it, is sending a report to the Main Staff of the HVO of Herceg-Bosna, and his assessment here is that the situation in town is deteriorating. He explains that this is after the Croatian flag was raised on the police station, there is a possibility of a large-scale conflict in town. According to the information from Novi Travnik, the HVO command there was shelled by the army of BH, and the conflict is underway. So on the 19th of October, this person is drawing attention to the deteriorating situation and providing some reasons for this. Would you agree that tensions could really be felt at the time? Will you please just say, "I agree," "I don't know," "Yes," "No," without comments, please. You have commented everything you possibly could today.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just going to say that. I have already repeated several times that this did happen in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So this document confirms that. The next document is 3D 00286, or in the bundle for the Court, 3D 110009. This is again the same person. You will see -- now it will come up on the screen. It's only a day later. And he is making a request from the HVO commander to make a defence plan for the town in coordination with the military police, a plan which could be used in case a conflict breaks out with the BH army. So it is evident from this that in his assessment a conflict is possible. You agreed that the situation was tense. Would you agree that this was a reasonable request? "Yes" or "No" or, "I don't know." Or "I can't comment." Whatever you like, just please don't go into further explanations, because we don't have time.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't have a collocutor here who could respond from these military and police structures. This has quite a different dimension. You are representing it one-sidedly, although it can be explained with good intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, but you told us in your previous testimony and today that you did have some information about the situation, because you were the, let's say political advisor to the Territorial Defence. So you were a well-informed person. But let's leave that aside. All my questions are very simple, and you can always reply with "I know," or "I don't know." On that same day, that same person is again drawing the attention of the HVO Brigade command to the fact that the situation is continuing to deteriorate again with reference to the flag, and again he says that large-scale conflicts might break out in the town. This is number 3D 00288, and for the Court 3D 110013. Can we just take a brief look at it, because it's practically identical in content, but I think that if this person insisted on the same facts more than once, he was really trying to draw attention to the threat. I think we can move on to the next document. I'll skip one. I don't think we need deal with that one. 3D 00049 is the next document I'd like, please, or 3D 030058 for the Court. While we're waiting for that document to appear on our screens, I'm going to tell you in advance that the document was issued and signed and compiled by the same person, the chief of security, HVO, on the 22nd of October, just one or two days later than the previous documents. That's his report. And he indicates to the headquarters of the brigade the following: He says that there are eight locations in town for which he feels are strongholds being prepared by the BH army or, rather, the Territorial Defence in town, and then he goes on to say: "On the territory of the towns there are strong forces which are hiding, mostly in civilian facilities and don't appear on the streets much, so that the members of our units gain the impression that they have given up on any kind of conflict, and this is just a trick." And then he specifies. "For the moment, we have noticed that they have strong nests in feature 54," which is to be -- which is on the map of the town. "They have a group of people on the ground floor, whereas there's another group of people constantly in the attic and have the post office targeted." Then there's another feature, 89. It is in a butcher's shop, Dizdarevic's butcher shop, where there are also sniper nests. And there are strong forces in the new cultural centre as well as throughout the area of Pogradje, Borovnica, and Ogolj, where there are exclusively Muslims. From the Ogolj settlement all the civilian population has been moved out, the women and children. Then he goes on to say that there is another stronghold in Gmici and Kulagici settlements, as well as around the main water reservoir in town at Krcma. Finally, at the bottom, there's an interesting observation in the penultimate sentence where he says that: "We'd like to draw your attention that since according to certain activities of the BiH staff and certain information, we can glean that the OS BiH could start initial conflicts, and according to this information, measures should be taken with respect to organising our units. Now, can you confirm that these formations that he enumerates at these locations were actually hidden there or not? Just say, "Yes, I do know about that," or, "No, I don't know," "They were there," "They were not there."

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm quite certain that that was not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Let's me now ask you this: Are you quite sure that the command of the Territorial Defence informed you regularly about all their activities and plans? A moment ago when my colleague cross-examined you, you had some reservations with respect to some of the allegations he made in his statements, and you let it be understood that that was his business. Now, do you know that he gave you timely information, truthful information? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll answer your first question first, then we'll come to the second part. Gmici is mentioned here. Gmici is a settlement in which 90 per cent of the inhabitants are Croats. There are just a few Muslim households, whereas you say that it was a stronghold.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you for an answer.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct, and I'm not quite sure that the commander informed me nor did I ask him to inform me about all the details, but the allegations in this text are absolutely untruthful. Not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hujdur, once again, please answer my questions and nothing else. Let me repeat: So you agree that you didn't need to have all the information. If I can go back to the transcript, I think those were your exact words. You said in line 21, "I'm not quite sure that the command informed me," et cetera." So that was the question, and that was your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: May we now have the next document, 3D 00048, and for the Court this is 3D 030055. And when it appears on our monitor, you'll be able to see that it was compiled once again by the same individual, that it is the same day, the 22nd of October, so he was very active. And from the title you can see that it is a report with respect to the passing of the OS BiH army through the Menjik checkpoint. To try and save time, I'll just summarise what it says. He says that the HVO was informed that that same night two buses would be passing by with -- of the BH army, returning from positions at Gornji Vakuf and that there should be no obstacles to them at the checkpoint. The buses arrived, and so on. They crossed the checkpoint, and having crossed the checkpoint, one turned towards the village of Pridvorci, escorted by a TAM, a small van, and the second with a police Golf-type car turned in the direction towards Gornji Vakuf, and they later on returned. So it's quite clear that the soldiers in the buses stayed on. And we can see from what he says later on that he considers that these were reinforcements that had been brought in. Is it true and correct that reinforcements and forces from Gornji Vakuf were indeed brought into the Gornji Vakuf area? Did you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know, and if the -- I did know something about that, but with the Court's permission, I'd like to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to allow you to do that. Just answer my questions and we'll get to that. Did you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But may I be allowed to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please refrain from doing that. Is it true and correct that reinforcements were brought in?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Right, you said No, No, it's not correct. That's fine, you've answered my question. You said that that wasn't correct information. Thank you. Now, the next document that I'd like to show the witness is 3D 00050, once again of the 22nd of October. For the Court to find its way is 3D 030060. We have the document on our screens. Take a look at it for yourself. You can see once again this same chief of security informing his superiors --

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it in English and it's very small print.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just a piece of information and explanation: This Mr. Luka Markesic who was chief of security of the Prozor municipality, did you know him? Did you hear about him, his name, or is this the first time that you see this name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not know him, but I heard his name. I didn't know him personally, though, although I did -- I have heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In one of your documents that we looked at today, he was mentioned as occupying that post as a security officer in the HVO, and to make things quite clear, the answer you gave to the President of the Trial Chamber, you said you heard about him. You heard of him. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Thank you. We have the document on the monitor. The chief of security says that strong forces of the OS BiH were noticed by the primary school at Bihanica [phoen] where the staff for the southern area of the territory was located. And he also says that they are fully on -- on full alert. And he also mentions the person from the first document, Rasim Pilav, that his arrival was noted with his family members as well as some other individuals from the Gracanica settlement. And finally - and this is an interesting point - the last sentence of this document says that according to information from Jablanica, there is a unit on full alert if it needs to act as reinforcements to the BH army in Prozor if an incident were to erupt. So this clearly indicates the readiness of the BH army and its preparedness. Can you confirm or refute whether this is the correct information, whether that's how it was?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right. Incorrect. So you know that that was incorrect, do you? My colleagues have just drawn my attention to something. In the document that you commented on today presented to you by the Prosecution, number -- the number is P 01656, the number of the document, on page 6 of that document you say that as for Thursday, the 22nd of October, a meeting of the wartime Presidency of the municipality had been scheduled. So quite obviously there must have been some activity in those premises, and you mention there the chief or, rather, the Croatian delegation represented by, and among others, you say a head of SIS HVO Luka Markesic. So you knew him. You knew of him.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew of him, but I didn't know him personally. That's a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now the next document I'd like to show the witness is 3D 00122, or for the Court, 3D 040006. When it appears on the monitor, you'll be able to see that that is a document issued by the Main Staff of the OS of the BH army. It says IKM Konjic. The 23rd of October, 1992, is the date, and it was signed by Jovan Divjak, the deputy chief the Main Staff of the BiH army. It's rather a long -- but let me ask you this first: Do you know the name of the chief of the Main Staff -- or of the deputy chief of the main staff, Jovan Divjak? Is that a familiar name to you?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is familiar but I didn't know the man. I don't know him personally, I know the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you, but you agree that he was a high-ranking officer in the Main Staff of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, this is a rather long document. It speaks for itself so I don't think it needs any great comment, but just briefly I'd like to indicate, and you can peruse the document yourself, it was sent to the commands of the Municipal Staff and Territorial Defence of Konjic, Jablanica and Prozor, and in the introductory paragraphs it assesses that the enemy has increased in strength, reinforced its forces throughout Nevesinje and Boracko Jezero, and so an attack can be expected along the axis of Boracko Jezero-Bijela-Konjic, et cetera. So my first question to you is who is the enemy? Does that the refer to the JNA or, rather, the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judges cannot find the document. What is the number at the bottom of the document, the reference number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be 3D 040006. The appearance is different. It is the army document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't seem to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution also cannot find the documents in its --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We obviously made some mistake. Then I would suggest that we would make a copy during the -- the session. Our case manager would go, because this is a really important document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead. Ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: There is too much papers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the usher to have another document, 3D 00123, placed on the -- on e-court. And it is 3D 040009 for the purposes of the Trial Chamber. And could we have prepared the following document because we're going to take it as a set of documents: 3D 00130, 00289, and 00283. And we'll give you the other numbers later on. [In English] I am afraid that is not the proper document. [Interpretation] The first document should be 3D 00123. [In English] No. No. It is not the proper one. Should be 00123. 3D -- 3D 00013. And for the Judges, that would be 3D 040009. That's the one. [Interpretation] Mr. Hujdur, would you cast your eyes on that document. We see that it says the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Defence Council, and so on and so forth in the heading. The 23rd of October was when it was compiled, and it was sent out to the military and civilian representative of the Muslims of Prozor municipality. Now, I do believe that you were probably one of the addressees of that document. Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should have been, but unfortunately I wasn't, and this is the first time I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Have you heard anything about it? Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Wasn't that the document discussed at the meeting that was mentioned in your extensive information?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because this calls for an urgent cease-fire, an unconditional cease-fire, whereas at that time there was no action going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. But the topic of discussion -- the topics of discussion were similar or the same as those set out here?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, here the Presidency of the HVO of Prozor and the heads of the brigades - we have the addressees as the military and civilian representatives of the Muslims in Prozor municipality - and it says, "Our proposals --" the subject is "Our proposals for overcoming the newly arisen political security situation." That is the day when you said that the meeting was interrupted and that the attack occurred. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, but this document was never disclosed, and it was not disclosed at this meeting either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see it there?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nor did anyone talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. Could we now please see document -- just a moment, please. We might be able to skip this one. No. No, we need it. Document 3D 00130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the Judges, what number is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's not here, but I believe that court officer will help me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We have this document on the monitor. Mr. Hujdur, have you seen it?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm looking at part of it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This document was compiled in the immediate aftermath of the incidents we have discussed at great length. Could the court officer please scroll up so that the signatures are visible. The signature, yes. Thank you. The 26th of October. It mentions the cease-fire that was established on the 25th of October, and in fact, this refers to an attempt to ensure the passage of a convoy of weapons going to Jajce where the situation is critical, the Chetniks are attacking with full force, and so on. And the signatory is the brigade commander Franjic. He orders a halt to all combat activity until further notice from all weapons and artillery pieces at all points. If attacked by the enemy, offer resistance, prevent looting, burning, and maltreatment of civilians. I believe that the document speaks for itself. Everybody can see it. And he is forwarding it to all the units under his command. So my first question to you is the following: For a long time previous to this, in view of the fact that Prozor is on the main road, the south-north road, there were regular passages of logistics and equipment for the fighting in Jajce along that road. Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in part, in a certain periods there were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And we agree, of course, that the forces the BH army and the forces of the HVO jointly endeavoured in heavy fighting to protect Jajce and prevent the breakthrough and taking of Jajce by the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I know what you're getting at, but can you confirm that in general both forces fought together?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a considerable period of time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, now I'll say what you were about to say. One side still accuses the other and blames the other side for the fall of Jajce; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that Jajce is not in our indictment, I will not go into this, but we agree that there is no understanding about the reasons why Jajce fell, for your consolation I will tell you that a top military expert says it was undefendable. But it's true that convoys passed through on their way to Jajce.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in a prior period to the one we are now referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you think that in this document there is an error when it says that there is a convoy going to Jajce? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It couldn't have passed through in this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're talking about October, it couldn't have passed through in that period. It could only have passed through earlier, a convoy for Jajce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's your opinion. A few days later, or before -- and the next document is 3D 00289. [In English] And I will soon advise the number for the Judges. For the Judges, that will be 3D 110015. [Interpretation] We have the document on the screen now. Four days before the previous document, this is a document signed by General Slobodan Praljak and Bruno Stojic -- Major General Praljak, and it's addressed to the commanders of the operative zones in Central Bosnia, Tihomir Blaskic and Stjepan Blazevic, the commander of the sector in Jajce. And it says that: "For 58 hours we have been trying to have an armed HVO formation go in the direction of Jajce consisting of about 400 armed soldiers. For now this group has on two occasions been prevented by the Muslim units from passing through in the direction of Jajce. Today I agreed that representatives of the HVO and the SDA should go jointly, together with the units with the HVO and the armed forces of the BH Territorial Defence, in order to solve the problems which have arisen and to enable our group or to pass through to towards Jajce. Please do your very best to calm down all the misunderstandings that have arisen with the Muslims in the areas of Novi Travnik and Fojnica, and use your influence on the Muslims to ensure unimpeded passage in the direction of Jajce." Were you informed by your party or the Territorial Defence about this, because it was widely distributed in a desire to make it possible for the convoy to pass through to Jajce. Were you informed about this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I say yes and give a short explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You may, but please make it brief.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Even some of the representatives of the HVO from Prozor put this question to us and asked us to go and mediate with the representatives of Gornji Vakuf, because that's where the alleged problem was. But somebody gave us information that these forces were not on their way to Jajce but, rather, to Novi Travnik. Jajce fell four or five days after Prozor. The explanation was that it was too late. But we promised our neighbours and colleagues the Croats that they would try to talk to our colleagues in Vakuf about this issue, too, with reference to Jajce. That's what I know and what we talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you did not prevent it, and there was an attempt to let it pass, pass through. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were willing to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know on the 23rd, when the conflict broke out, were any of these transports to Jajce sent back to Prozor because they couldn't go any further than Gornji Vakuf? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know any details. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: For example, that armoured personnel carrier you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in front of the police station on the 23rd. I saw it myself. It couldn't have come back, not that particular one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document. That's 3D 00126, or for Their Honours, 3D 040020. And let me first ask you, while we're waiting for the document to come up, it was signed by the chief of the brigade on the 23rd or on the 24th of October in Prozor municipality. His name was Petar Kolakusic. Do you know him or anything about him?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Was he a local person from Prozor?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you know that he actually was the chief in the brigade command at the time? You nodded. For the sake of the record, could you say yes?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was trying to look at the contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, I was only asking you about the signature. So you do confirm that you know this person and that he was the chief in the brigade staff?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: When you nod, it's not recorded in the record. So we see here there is mention first of a murder, unfortunately. This time a member of the HVO, Frano Zadro, was killed. And this is to do with what my colleague asked you about. It was the immediate cause for the interruption of the meeting. You said that no HVO soldier had been killed and that could not have been a reason for the interruption of that meeting, but here again we have a document confirming that information. It's a document reporting on this incident. It says that, "HVO member Frano Zadro, in the area of Crni Vrh, just when the two sides were having talks about resolving the situation such as it is, was perfidiously killed." We have this on the monitor now, and we see that this document was compiled very fast, and it says that the town is under the control of the police forces of the HVO. Assistance is sought in manpower due to exhaustion as well as armoured units to maintain peace in the town. There is no adequate person for negotiations, either military or political. It's currently quiet. There are quite a few prisoners, members of the BH armed forces. On our side one dead, one missing, five slightly wounded. On the other side several killed and wounded. And the prisoners were found to possess arsenals of the most modern weaponry which never was nor would be used against the Chetniks but only against us. Are you aware of any of this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in part, where it talks about control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document I wish to show is 3D 00125. It's already an exhibit. And for the Court it's 3D 040107. We have the document on the screen now. It's hard to see the date, but we think it's the 24th of October. It was signed by Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic, here present, and I think it speaks for itself. It concerns a cessation of hostilities and it's an express order, and reporting is required to keep order. Did you hear about such a document arriving in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Prozor, you mean? No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said in Gornji Vakuf. You meant to say Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I did mean Prozor.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not hear about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We see that this document was sent to all the towns in the area: Prozor, Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Vitez, Konjic, Tomislavgrad and Travnik. The next document is 3D 00131, or for Their Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May I just --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: -- make an observation for the record. The document you have just referred to and you have said was 3D 040107, I refer to line 3 of page 103, we have it under the name 3D 040017. That's why I only found it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the document. As you can see, there are often errors in the record where numbers are concerned. I am trying to read them slowly. Let me get out another document and then we'll come back to the one we sent for copying.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. [Interpretation] The document 3D 000122, for the Judges 3D 040006 for the Judges. We've just sent it to be copied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, the witness knows about this. This is a BH army document signed, once again, by Jovan Divjak. You'll see when we get to that. But I'd just like to indicate certain details. The date is the 23rd of October, in the evening, and according to what we heard, this is while the fighting was going on in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We have the introduction, introductory remarks telling us about the situation. I don't want to tire you with that now. The only thing I'm interested in is something on the next page, page 2. May I have the next page shown on the monitor. It is point 3.3. And there we have a task relating to the Municipal Staff of the defence of Prozor which must defend the present positions, and when the battalion of the Municipal Staff of the defence of Jablanica arrives should prevent taking control of Prozor and undertake measures that the forces must be repelled from the Prozor municipality territory. So the highest staff of the BH army is issuing instructions about what must be done, and this order presupposes the fact that sufficient forces exist which can fight the HVO on a footing of equality. And if what you told us is correct about the strength of the HVO and the strength of the BH army, and my colleague asked you about that today, no military commander would issue this kind of instruction. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. Quite obviously this person didn't have an overall view of the situation. Quite obviously he wasn't on top of the situation, in control of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you believe that Divjak did not have sufficient information about the actual deployment of forces in Prozor.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. May I have the next document, please, 3D 00131. For the Judges 3D 040032. It's a very short document, two days after the conflict ended. Once again, Petar Kolakusic is the signatory. I think the document speaks for itself. Did you hear that the HVO tried to stop the activities, suppress the activities of those individuals who were -- had escaped control? And this refers to attempts to prevent any burning or infliction of damage.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A brief answer, if possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, go on.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that this was an oral decision also given by General Praljak, and that's a good order. But how events developed in the field is quite different, is a different matter altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. We can speak about that and the reasons for that later on, but we see that there was an attempt to put things right. Next document, please, 3D 0021. I'm sorry, 291, 00291. I misspoke. And for the Judges, this would be number 3D 110024. This is another report from the chief of security, this time signed or, rather, initialed and somebody else worked with him. He needed some help. And we're in December there, after the conflict and after the meeting of the 1st of December attended by General Praljak that you spoke of earlier on. I'd like to draw your attention to the following -- Have you had a chance to look through the document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's just come up on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Straight at the beginning of the document we see that it says: "In the past couple of days after the arrival General Slobodan Praljak many things have changed in Prozor, or are changing in Prozor. General Praljak, on the 30th of December, 1992, arrived in Prozor and upon his arrival straight away --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, may I just draw your attention to the fact that this document is dated 8 December and speaks of a visit of General Praljak of 30 December. It's a prophetic document or is something wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was just going to mention that this must be a typing error, because it was written on the 8th of December dealing with the previous week, and from earlier exhibits we saw that General Praljak held a meeting on the 1st of December. So he arrived in Prozor on the evening of the 30th of November. That's what it is, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we'll be able to see that later on from the next portion, next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So everybody -- everybody takes note that General Praljak arrived, and upon his arrival he immediately orders that a group of prisoners be set free, amongst whom was Salih Ruvic, commander of the BH army under whose leadership during the conflict in Prozor the first front line of the OS BiH units left, and a criminal report was filed against him. So that is the person that you mentioned had been brought to the meeting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So we can confirm the exactitude of the information there.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the section that -- well, there are parts here that don't reflect the truth, but some other parts do. And when it comes to them -- when it's a question of the man and the meeting with the general, then that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you confirm that Praljak -- that Ruvic and the other group of people were released and brought to the meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We can also see further down in the document a brief description of the meeting where mention is made of the second part of the meeting held in the motel. You spoke about that. It says that there were 1 -- about 150 people present and that it lasted for -- very briefly, that "The general informed all those present about the factual state of the situation and the interests of the Croatian people. The accent was placed on improving relations between the Croats and Muslims and the return of the Muslim populace to the territory of the municipality." This figure of people attending the meeting at -- the second meeting in the motel, does that correspond to the number of people that were there?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I don't think that many people could have fitted into the room in the motel. I think this figure was exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, when we spoke of the meeting, we omitted a detail. Among other things, would you agree or, rather, did you happen to notice, do you know that at the meeting also present were what we like to say the elders of the village, that is to say wise elderly men and that each of the villages sent two elders to attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know about the three or four villagers that I mentioned today, Scipe, Here, and Kute.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But you allow that that was true of other villages too?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't deny it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. There are some other details but I don't think we need to go into them. Next document, please. 3D 00290. For the Judges, 3D 110019.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak. We have five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the -- we're dealing with two meetings, one meeting that was held when the gentleman was there, which I interrupted because they had beaten up Ruvic, and then I convened a meeting for the next day where I invited all the Croats from all the villages, two of them from each village, a large meeting where I tried to explain the situation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, we just heard that explanation. You didn't attend the second meeting?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Just the two meetings in UNIS and at the motel on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the truth of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But do you know about that second meeting?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You'll see later on from the signature on the next page this document was signed by Major General Slobodan Praljak. It was issued on paper heading of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna on the 6th of November, 1992. So that was a little after the conflict. And the reason I'm showing you this document is that it was addressed to all the representatives and members of the HVO and BH army. Now, you in your capacity as member of that board of yours, did you have an opportunity to see the document? Perhaps you were informed of the document. Take a look at its contents. Perhaps it will help jog your memory. According to our information, the Territorial Defence sent it out broadly to everyone, to the army too.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 6th of November. That's the 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could not have been physically in a position to receive the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I thought you were at Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Jablanica but never received this document. So perhaps that is the result of those activities and the activities of the meeting of the 1st of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: All right. But if you take a look at the document, and you can see it on your screen, the fact is that the convoys and passage of convoys with all logistics for both armies and humanitarian supplies, passed by all the checkpoints unimpeded. Do you remember that the situation was very good at the beginning of November?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I remember is the following: During that period of time a convoy of people from Jajce passed by, because Jajce had unfortunately already fallen, and I remember that, because it was a very sad column, just like the column we were in several days before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps have a chance to read point 4 at the end of page 1? And it required certain activities on your part. Perhaps that can remind you. That is to set up mixed patrols for the control of movement and the behaviour of members of the military units. So parity is asked in point 10 on the second page. Look at point 10 where Praljak orders -- point 10 is particularly interesting, although it's indicated in point 8 as well, that the administration of the military police and HVO police, the army will secure 64 members of the military police of the HVO and army of BH army according to an ethnic parity for the need of working in the Prozor municipality region.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can say something briefly about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these efforts did give certain results. We heard about this attempt for a joint police from Mostar to Prozor, but unfortunately they didn't supply a flag, and fortunately they returned, but the situation improved until the beginning of January when it began to deteriorate with the attack on Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that there was less pressure or, rather, there was pressure from General Praljak for peace and that, after that, the situation became out of control?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
