utterances.text: The situation certainly became out of control. If General Praljak was less active there, then that would be true. Perhaps they listened to him less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have four or five more documents, but quite obviously our time seems to be up. I consider them to be relevant. Might I be allowed to have an extra 15 minutes tomorrow morning? My colleague wanted to have a few minutes for himself, but he's given up on that idea. Or perhaps I could just tender them as a passage deal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are telling us that the problem that will arise tomorrow is that we have a witness whom we should hear for four hours, and tomorrow we will have four hours and 45 minutes. So the Prosecution will have to cut down on its time. And you yourselves, you will have to make an effort also, because if you need 15 minutes plus I don't know how much time for the other Defence counsel. How much time will the other Defence counsel need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can see for yourself all the other Defence counsel say they don't need anything more. They don't want to take up any more time, have nothing to ask. I'll need 15 minutes. The witness is cooperative, so I think that I'll be able to get through some of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So ideally we should finish today so that the witness can leave. So we shall continue for another 15 minutes. I think everybody needs to be adaptable here. So we shall stay in court for another 15 minutes. Please make it short. And I hope that the Prosecution has no questions, extra questions to put to the witness. No redirect examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3D 000137 is the next document I'd like to have displayed. And for the Judges, the number is 3D 040064. I do apologise. For Their Honours it will be 0070. 3D 040070 is the number of the document for the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to appear on our screens, Mr. Hujdur -- it's already on the monitor, on the screen. This is once again a document from the Rama headquarters. It is a report, we can see that from the title, to the Main Staff. Pursuant order such-and-such from the Main Staff. So the Main Staff has asked to see what happened exactly in Prozor. Of course we don't have enough time to go through all that and deal with the document in its entirety. I'd just like to draw your attention to page 3 of this document. In the upper right-hand corner you will find the page numbers, ERN number -- yes, that's right. And at the bottom of that page, point 4 is the one I'd like to look at. Inter alia, the document states that as for casualties, 11 were killed on the BH army side, five on the HVO side, 18 HVO members were wounded, an unknown number of members of the TO were wounded. Some TO members were hospitalised in the war hospital in Rumboci. An unidentified number of houses was destroyed, but mostly houses from which HVO troops were attacked. On the other side, the parish house and the Municipal Council building in Prozor were damaged. Would you agree that among those killed and wounded the figures are correct and that this information was checked?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brief answer to this is that in the town of Prozor no soldiers on the Bosnian side were killed. All those killed were civilians. The soldier killed here was killed outside the town of Prozor, a few kilometres away. I can't speak about HVO members, but this is completely incorrect and untrue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Very well. One more document. The document is 3D 00292. For Their Honours, 3D 110027. Mr. Hujdur, when you see the document on your screen -- here it is. In the upper right-hand corner we see the date is the 29th of March, 1993. You mentioned that when an incident occurred on the 28th of August, damages were paid to people. Here we see a document where we see that Professor Jozic, the president of the HVO, signed the document. You mentioned him. We agree that he was the president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this is the document from 1993. The incident we talked about on the 28th of August took place in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's correct. I was just reminding you of that event where the municipality paid damages to people.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, now I'm putting this document to you. It refers to damage caused before the 29th of March, 1993. Commissions were established to determine what the damage was. This was published in the Municipal Gazette. Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot deny that it was published, but we did not have access to the Municipal Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Do you know any people who were paid damages based on this?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Maybe if you take a look at the composition of the municipal commission, if you look at the names, do you see that it was a multi-ethnic commission comprising both Croats and Muslims? Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Also, the expert commission in Article 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I don't see that. Could the document be scrolled up, please. Could we scroll up a bit? Yes. Thank you. Under Article 2 it says Munereva Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: She is a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. So we agree that it was multi-ethnic?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you say expert. She was obviously no expert, but maybe she was able to do the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, if you take a good look at the text, the two commissions have different tasks. But you do agree that both commissions were multi-ethnic and that they dealt with war damage. I would now like to show one more document in connection with this. It's 3D 00138, or for Their Honours, 3D 040078. The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Official Gazette. On the right-hand side there is a decree on establishing war damage on the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and that's number 4 from August, 1992, and the legal basis of the document we have seen is this decree enacted by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. The municipalities then, based on this decree, issued their own decrees for the compensation of damages when this was needed. Have you seen this decree?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: But it was published in the Official Gazette. Thank you very much. And just one more document since we are so short of time. 3D 00136, and for Their Honours, 3D 040064. It's a very brief document, so it won't take up a lot of time. Can we zoom in a bit? This is a document issued by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Main Staff of the HVO, HZ HB, 31st of October, 1992. The heading is the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Croatian Community, the Croatian Defence Council. It's signed by the chief of the main HVO staff, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic, and he quite clearly and unambiguously requires discipline, establishes that there is information, that houses are being burnt and destroyed in the Prozor municipality, Muslim houses. He demands that all means be used to prevent such behaviour. He draws attention to the fact that this will cause enormous problems because of international media, and he says that in every place an intervention group of conscientious people should be set up to prevent this because obviously the existing structures don't have the strength to do that. Have you had occasion to see this document?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, not. But if I were a formalist, I would challenge it because I don't see a stamp or a signature here. However, I will not be such a formalist. Here one can see what legal action should have been taken but was not carried through on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For Their Honours, this document was found in the national archives of Croatia. This particular copy was found by the Office of the Prosecutor, and we know from other cases that Paket communications were used and all such documents have no stamp or signature. That's what documents sent by Paket communications look like. Your Honours, I have two or three further documents, but in order to contribute to expeditiousness, we will not present them. I have one final question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Be quick, be quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Now that you've seen a lot of new information, would you agree that in fact the distribution of forces in Prozor was such that they were simply waiting for the other side to begin? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Never. Neither I nor others in my impression did -- ever wanted or expected such a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Well, do you see any indications in these documents that the army was preparing for a conflict with the HVO and they may have been planning an attack? Were there preparations to this effect on the part of the army?

utterances.speaker: OMER HUJDUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the Defence of the town is in question, was it ever said that they would not defend the town regardless of who was attacking it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's your comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I do apologise, but thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. No redirect from the Prosecution, Mr. Kruger?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we did have more time I indeed actually did have three questions. However, I think that the responses that would be elicited have actually been dealt with by the witness in other parts of his evidence, so I will not put more questions at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Kovacic, you would like the exhibits to be tendered into evidence? We won't do this now because we don't have any more time left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I intentionally left this for tomorrow morning. We're all tired now. It's 5.30. By your leave, of course, I would prefer to do it tomorrow morning and have the list on a piece of paper. It will be much faster and more expeditious. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So I note that there are no more questions from the Defence, and the Prosecution is not going to ask any additional questions. The Judges have no more questions, and they are not exhausted -- they have not exhausted the questions they wanted to put. So I, on behalf of my fellow Judge and myself, we would like to wish you a safe journey home, and the usher will accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, and all the best to you, although I expected I could address you, but obviously that's not envisioned in the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask the registrar to move into private session for a few minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are currently in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in open session I would like to state that the hearing will resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning, and we shall hear a witness testify tomorrow morning. I wish you a nice evening. The court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of June, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.33 p.m.,
